# zeroclaw
## HarnessBench adapter
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

from harnessbench.adapters.base import BaseAdapter
from harnessbench.models import AdapterRunContext, AdapterRunResult
from harnessbench.usage_proxy import register_routes


def _project_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _resolve_project_path(raw: str | Path) -> Path:
    p = Path(os.path.expanduser(str(raw)))
    if not p.is_absolute():
        p = _project_root() / p
    return p.resolve()


def _copy_if_exists(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if src.is_dir():
        shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True)
    else:
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def _render_toml_string_array(values: list[str]) -> str:
    rendered_lines = ["["]
    rendered_lines.extend(f'    "{item}",' for item in values)
    rendered_lines.append("]")
    return "\n".join(rendered_lines)


def _upsert_autonomy_value(block: str, key: str, rendered_value: str) -> str:
    pattern = re.compile(rf"(?ms)^\s*{re.escape(key)}\s*=\s*(?:\[(?:.*?\n)*?\s*\]|[^\n]+)")
    replacement = f"{key} = {rendered_value}"
    if pattern.search(block):
        return pattern.sub(replacement, block, count=1)
    return block.rstrip() + f"\n{replacement}\n"


def _upsert_top_level_string(raw: str, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    pattern = re.compile(rf'(?m)^{re.escape(key)}\s*=\s*"[^"\n]*"')
    replacement = f'{key} = "{value}"'
    if pattern.search(raw):
        return pattern.sub(replacement, raw, count=1)
    return replacement + "\n" + raw


def _merge_user_config(
    user_config: Path,
    out_path: Path,
    *,
    workspace: Path,
    sandbox: Path,
    zeroclaw_home: Path,
    proxy_base_url: str = "",
    proxy_routes_file: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    raw = user_config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    data = tomllib.loads(raw)
    text = raw

    default_provider = str(data.get("default_provider") or "").strip()
    if proxy_base_url and proxy_routes_file is not None:
        provider_prefix = ""
        upstream = ""
        if default_provider.startswith("custom:"):
            provider_prefix = "custom"
            upstream = default_provider[len("custom:"):].strip()
        elif default_provider.startswith("anthropic-custom:"):
            provider_prefix = "anthropic-custom"
            upstream = default_provider[len("anthropic-custom:"):].strip()

        if upstream:
            route_prefix = "/zeroclaw/default"
            register_routes(
                proxy_routes_file,
                {
                    route_prefix: {
                        "framework": "zeroclaw",
                        "provider": "default",
                        "upstream": upstream,
                    }
                },
            )
            text = _upsert_top_level_string(
                text,
                "default_provider",
                f"{provider_prefix}:{proxy_base_url}{route_prefix}",
            )

    autonomy = data.setdefault("autonomy", {})
    allowed_roots = autonomy.get("allowed_roots")
    root_entries = list(allowed_roots) if isinstance(allowed_roots, list) else []
    root_values = [str(item) for item in root_entries]
    dynamic_roots = [
        str(path.resolve())
        for path in (workspace, sandbox, zeroclaw_home)
    ]
    for root in dynamic_roots:
        if root not in root_values:
            root_values.append(root)
    allowed_roots_value = _render_toml_string_array(root_values)

    autonomy_section = re.search(r"(?ms)^\[autonomy\]\n(.*?)(?=^\[|\Z)", text)
    if autonomy_section:
        block = autonomy_section.group(0)
        updated_block = _upsert_autonomy_value(block, "allowed_roots", allowed_roots_value)
        text = text[: autonomy_section.start()] + updated_block + text[autonomy_section.end() :]
    else:
        text = (
            text.rstrip()
            + "\n\n[autonomy]\n"
            + f"allowed_roots = {allowed_roots_value}\n"
        )
    out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


class ZeroClawAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    name = "zeroclaw"

    def run(self, ctx: AdapterRunContext) -> AdapterRunResult:
        command = str(ctx.model_config.get("command") or "zeroclaw")
        user_config_raw = str(ctx.model_config.get("user_config") or "config/zeroclaw.toml")
        user_config = _resolve_project_path(user_config_raw)
        if not user_config.is_file():
            return AdapterRunResult(ok=False, stderr=f"missing ZeroClaw source config: {user_config}")

        isolated_home = ctx.sandbox
        zeroclaw_home = isolated_home / ".zeroclaw"
        zeroclaw_home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Encrypted `enc2:` secrets are keyed by `<config_dir>/.secret_key`.
        config_secret_key = user_config.parent / ".secret_key"
        _copy_if_exists(config_secret_key, zeroclaw_home / ".secret_key")

        zeroclaw_workspace = zeroclaw_home / "workspace"
        zeroclaw_workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        sandbox_user_config = zeroclaw_home / "config.src.toml"
        shutil.copy2(user_config, sandbox_user_config)
        merged_cfg = zeroclaw_home / "config.toml"
        _merge_user_config(
            sandbox_user_config,
            merged_cfg,
            workspace=ctx.workspace,
            sandbox=ctx.sandbox,
            zeroclaw_home=zeroclaw_home,
            proxy_base_url=str(ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_URL") or ""),
            proxy_routes_file=Path(ctx.env["HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES"]) if ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES") else None,
        )

        session_state_dir = zeroclaw_home / "sessions"
        session_state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        session_state_file = session_state_dir / f"{ctx.session_id}.json"

        cmd = [
            command,
            "--config-dir",
            str(zeroclaw_home),
            "agent",
            "--session-state-file",
            str(session_state_file),
            "-m",
            ctx.prompt,
        ]
        provider = str(ctx.model_config.get("provider") or "").strip()
        if provider:
            cmd.extend(["--provider", provider])
        extra_args = [str(x) for x in (ctx.model_config.get("extra_args") or [])]
        if extra_args:
            cmd.extend(extra_args)

        env = os.environ.copy()
        env.update(ctx.env)
        env["HOME"] = str(isolated_home)
        env["WORKSPACE"] = str(ctx.workspace)
        env["ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR"] = str(zeroclaw_home)
        env["ZEROCLAW_WORKSPACE"] = str(zeroclaw_workspace)
        env["ZEROCLAW_HOME"] = str(zeroclaw_home)
        env["ZEROCLAW_SESSION_ID"] = ctx.session_id

        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            cwd=str(ctx.workspace),
            text=True,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=ctx.timeout_sec,
            env=env,
            check=False,
        )
        return AdapterRunResult(
            ok=completed.returncode == 0,
            command=cmd,
            stdout=completed.stdout,
            stderr=completed.stderr,
            metadata={
                "returncode": completed.returncode,
                "zeroclaw_config_path": str(merged_cfg),
                "source_user_config_path": str(user_config),
                "sandbox_user_config_path": str(sandbox_user_config),
                "isolated_home": str(isolated_home),
                "zeroclaw_home": str(zeroclaw_home),
                "zeroclaw_workspace": str(zeroclaw_workspace),
                "session_state_file": str(session_state_file),
                "workspace": str(ctx.workspace),
            },
        )

<h1 align="center">🦀 ZeroClaw — Personal AI Assistant</h1>

<p align="center">
  <strong>You own the agent. You own the data. You own the machine it runs on.</strong>
</p>

---

ZeroClaw is an agent runtime — a single Rust binary you configure and run. It talks to LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and ~20 others), reaches the world through 30+ channels (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, email, voice, webhooks, your own CLI), and acts through tools (shell, browser, HTTP, hardware, custom MCP servers). Everything runs on your machine, with your keys, in your workspace.

Read the [Philosophy](docs/book/src/philosophy/index.md) for the four opinions that shape it.

## Install

### Unix (recommended)

<!-- >>> generated:readme-unix-fast by `cargo generate installers` - do not edit <<< -->
```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/master/install.sh | sh
"${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin/zeroclaw" quickstart
```
<!-- >>> end generated:readme-unix-fast <<< -->

### Windows (recommended)

Use the Rust-free [prebuilt PowerShell path](docs/book/src/setup/windows.md#option-1-prebuilt-binary-recommended) in the Windows setup guide. It installs the current release, updates PATH, and runs Quickstart.

For the guided Unix installer, source builds, app and feature selection, and PATH behavior, compare the [installation paths](docs/book/src/getting-started/quickstart.md#install).

Run `./install.sh --help` for the complete Unix installer flag reference.

> **Working on the docs?** The translated documentation catalogues live in a
> git submodule (`docs/book/po`). The Rust build does not need it, but building
> or syncing the docs does. Clone with it, or add it to an existing clone:
>
> ```bash
> git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw.git
> git submodule update --init docs/book/po   # existing clone
> ```

Platform-specific notes: [Linux](docs/book/src/setup/linux.md) · [macOS](docs/book/src/setup/macos.md) · [Windows](docs/book/src/setup/windows.md) · [FreeBSD](docs/book/src/setup/freebsd.md) · [NixOS](docs/book/src/setup/nixos.md) · [Docker](docs/book/src/setup/container.md)

## Quick start

```bash
zeroclaw quickstart               # one-shot setup: pick a provider, write a working config
zeroclaw agent -a <alias>         # interactive chat using the [agents.<alias>] entry
zeroclaw service install          # register as systemd/launchctl/Windows Service
zeroclaw service start            # run it always-on in the background
```

Full walkthrough: [Quick start](docs/book/src/getting-started/quickstart.md) — or skip the safety gates with [YOLO mode](docs/book/src/getting-started/yolo.md) for dev boxes.

## What ZeroClaw does

- **Multi-channel** — one agent answering you across [every channel you configure](docs/book/src/channels/overview.md). Inbound messages from Discord, Telegram, Matrix, email, webhooks, CLI — all delivered to the same agent loop.
- **Provider-agnostic** — [model providers](docs/book/src/providers/overview.md) are pluggable. Configure Anthropic, OpenAI, local Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. [Fallback chains and routing](docs/book/src/providers/routing.md) keep the agent running when a provider flakes.
- **Security-first, with escape hatches** — default autonomy is `supervised`: medium-risk ops require approval, high-risk blocked. Workspace boundaries, command policy, OS-level sandboxes (Landlock / Bubblewrap / Seatbelt / Docker), and cryptographic [tool receipts](docs/book/src/security/tool-receipts.md) on every action. [YOLO mode](docs/book/src/getting-started/yolo.md) exists for trusted dev environments.
- **Hardware-capable** — GPIO / I2C / SPI / USB on Raspberry Pi, STM32, Arduino, and ESP32 via the `Peripheral` trait. See [Hardware](docs/book/src/hardware/index.md).
- **Gateway + dashboard** — HTTP / WebSocket gateway for clients, with a web dashboard for chat, memory browsing, config editing, cron management, and tool inspection.
- **SOP engine** — event-triggered [Standard Operating Procedures](docs/book/src/sop/index.md) (MQTT / webhook / cron / peripheral) with approval gates and resumable runs.
- **ACP** — IDE / editor integration via [Agent Client Protocol](docs/book/src/channels/acp.md) (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio).

## Configuration

One TOML file at `~/.zeroclaw/config.toml`. Pointers:

- [Provider configuration](docs/book/src/providers/configuration.md) — the universal `[providers.models.<type>.<alias>]` schema
- [Channels overview](docs/book/src/channels/overview.md) — per-channel `[channels.<type>.<alias>]` blocks
- [Security overview](docs/book/src/security/overview.md) — autonomy, sandboxing, tool receipts
- [Full config reference](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/reference/config.html) — generated from the live schema; every key documented

A V3 config has at minimum four section headers (`<type>.<alias>` shaped) — a provider entry, an agent that references it, and a risk profile the agent gates against. See [Provider Configuration → Minimal working example](docs/book/src/providers/configuration.md#minimal-working-example) for the canonical four-section form with inline type/alias commentary.

For standard OpenAI Codex subscription auth, Quickstart can write the provider
entry for you:

```bash
zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json  # if already signed in with Codex CLI
zeroclaw quickstart --model-provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.4
```

The provider entry uses the canonical OpenAI shape; the alias below is an
example:

```toml
[providers.models.openai.coding]   # type = openai; alias = coding (you choose)
model = "gpt-5.4"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
```

…and point your agent at it with `model_provider = "openai.<alias>"`.

Notes:

- Normal OpenAI Codex subscription auth uses stored auth profiles, not an `api_key` on the provider entry.
- Claude Max setup-token auth stays on the canonical Anthropic slot: run `claude setup-token`, choose `setup_token` in Quickstart, and paste the generated token into the API key/token prompt.
- Only set `api_key` / `uri` on `[providers.models.openai.<alias>]` when intentionally targeting a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway or endpoint.
- If you see `provider streaming failed, falling back to non-streaming chat`, ZeroClaw retries the same request in non-streaming mode. Check `zeroclaw auth status` before changing provider config.

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            channels       gateway        ACP                 │
│          (30+ adapters)   (REST/WS)    (JSON-RPC)            │
│                        ↓                                     │
│                   ZeroClaw runtime                           │
│         ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐                   │
│         │  agent   │ security │   SOP    │                   │
│         │   loop   │  policy  │  engine  │                   │
│         └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘                   │
│              ↓          ↓           ↓                        │
│          providers    tools      memory                      │
│         (Anthropic,  (shell,    (SQLite,                     │
│          OpenAI,     browser,    embeddings)                 │
│          Ollama,     HTTP,                                   │
│          ~20 more)   hardware)                               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Full detail with Mermaid diagrams: [Architecture overview](docs/book/src/architecture/overview.md) · [Request lifecycle](docs/book/src/architecture/request-lifecycle.md) · [Crates](docs/book/src/architecture/crates.md).

## Contributing

Start with [how to contribute](docs/book/src/contributing/how-to.md). Larger changes go through the [RFC process](docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md). Real-time chat lives on [Discord](https://discord.gg/zeroclaw) (the best way to reach the team); durable work tracking is on [GitHub issues](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues).

Good places to start:

- New channel → `crates/zeroclaw-channels/`
- New provider → `crates/zeroclaw-providers/`
- New tool → `crates/zeroclaw-tools/`
- Hardware support → `crates/zeroclaw-hardware/`
- Docs → `docs/book/src/`

AI-assisted PRs are welcome; see [Contribution culture (RFC #5615)](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/5615) for the co-authorship norms.

## Security

Do not file public issues for security vulnerabilities. Email `security@zeroclaw.dev`. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the full policy.

## Official repository & impersonation notice

This is the only official ZeroClaw repository:

> <https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw>

Any other repository, organization, domain, or package claiming to be "ZeroClaw" or implying affiliation with ZeroClaw Labs is **unauthorized and not affiliated with this project**.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/discord.md-94-## Streaming

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-47-- Delivers new posts in near-real-time (no 3-second poll delay).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-48-- Reduces HTTP load on the Mattermost server (one connection vs. N polls/3s).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:49:- Returns failed sessions to the shared channel supervisor, which reconnects with bounded exponential backoff using the configured `reliability.channel_initial_backoff_secs` and `reliability.channel_max_backoff_secs` values.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-50-- Requires Mattermost v4.0+ (the `/api/v4/websocket` endpoint).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-51-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-55-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-56-- WebSocket mode must maintain a persistent TCP+TLS connection.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:57:- During a reconnect window, messages posted to a channel may be missed because this listener does not yet request Mattermost connection resume/replay. Polling catches up via `since=` cursors.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-58-- Polling mode is more resilient to transient network interruptions at the cost of constant HTTP traffic.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-60-To roll back, set `listen_mode = "polling"` (or remove the field; polling is the default).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-61-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:62:## Tool approval over chat (`approval_timeout_secs`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-63-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:64:When a tool needs approval (it is in `always_ask`, or the risk profile does not auto-approve it), the agent posts the request into the channel the message came from and waits. There are two ways to answer, and which ones you get depends on `listen_mode`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-65-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-66-**Reply with the token.** This works in every listen mode:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-68-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-69-APPROVAL REQUIRED [a1b2c3]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:70:Tool: shell
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-71-Args: command: pwd
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-72-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-84-**Tap a reaction.** This one requires `listen_mode = "websocket"`. The bot puts ✅ and ❌ on its own prompt post; tapping one answers it. Reactions reach the bot as `reaction_added` WebSocket events, and the polling listener reads posts and never sees them, so **under `listen_mode = "polling"` no emoji are seeded**: a button that silently does nothing on a security prompt is worse than no button. If you want one-tap approvals, set `listen_mode = "websocket"` (see [WebSocket mode](#websocket-mode)).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-85-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:86:`always` has no emoji on purpose. It grants a session-scoped allowlist entry rather than permitting a single call, and a mis-tap next to ✅ is too cheap a way to widen a session, so escalating to `always` stays a typed decision.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-87-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-88-Mattermost does not offer interactive message *buttons* here. Those post to an integration URL, which requires an inbound HTTP endpoint the bot has no way to expose from a polling or WebSocket client; reactions are the one-tap affordance that works over the connection the bot already holds.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-90-**Who may answer, and where.** The token is a correlator, not a password: it travels in plaintext into the channel, so every member can read it. Two conditions therefore both have to hold. The answering user must be in the alias's [peer group](./peer-groups.md), the same authority that decides whose messages the agent will act on. And the answer must arrive in the channel the prompt was posted into: one bot serves many channels, so a token carried into a different room is not an answer there, even from an authorized user. Binding is per channel rather than per thread, so replying in the channel instead of inside the prompt's thread is fine. A reply or tap that fails either check is logged at `WARN` and ignored, and the prompt stays open so an authorized operator can still answer it in the right place.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-91-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:92:**Everyone in the channel can read the tool arguments.** The prompt includes the tool name and a summary of its arguments. Route approvals to a channel whose membership you are comfortable showing those to.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-93-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:94:`approval_timeout_secs` bounds the wait. **The default is 300 seconds, and `0` denies immediately** rather than disabling approval, so a zero is a way to refuse every gated tool, not a way to wait forever. On timeout the request is denied and the token is discarded, so a late reply or tap cannot approve a call nobody is waiting on any more. A timeout or an unreachable prompt is recorded as the runtime denying on its own authority, not as a human refusing.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-95-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-96-Decisions are final: removing a reaction does not retract an answer, and the first valid answer retires the prompt for both paths.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-101-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-102-Off by default. When enabled, each room's Mattermost **channel purpose** is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:103:injected into the agent's system prompt as channel-supplied context, so one
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-104-room can specialise the agent without a config entry per room:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-105-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-116-labelled as channel-supplied and explicitly denied any power to grant
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-117-capabilities, relax restrictions, or override operating rules; where it
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:118:conflicts with them, the rules win. It cannot enable a tool, widen a peer
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-119-group, or change an autonomy level.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-120-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-147-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-148-What the purpose still cannot do is *widen* those capabilities. It cannot enable
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:149:a tool, add a peer, change an autonomy level, or approve its own tool call:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-150-those are decided by config and by the approval path, neither of which reads

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:199:{{#thread-context channel="Mattermost" prop="thread_replies" path="channels.mattermost.<alias>.thread_replies"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-200-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-201-## Authentication
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-204-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-205-1. **Bot token** (preferred). Create at **System Console → Integrations → Bot Accounts**, copy the access token, store it in `bot_token`. Tokens survive password rotations and are easier to revoke.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:206:2. **Login flow**. Set `login_id` (email or username) and `password`. The bot calls `POST /api/v4/users/login` on startup and caches the returned session token in memory. No persistence to disk.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-207-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-208-`bot_token` wins when both are set.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-224-1. Poll cadence is 3 seconds per channel. N discovered channels = N HTTP calls every 3 seconds against the Mattermost server. Self-hosted defaults handle this easily; if you're on a shared cloud tenant with tight rate limits, consider scoping with `channel_ids` or `team_ids`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-225-2. The bot identity is fetched once via `GET /api/v4/users/me` and cached for the process lifetime. Username changes require a restart.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md:226:3. The session token from the password login flow is in-memory only. A restart re-logs in.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-227-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/mattermost.md-228-## See also
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-29-  ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-30-- **Bot secret** from that installation. Nextcloud issues **one** shared secret per
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md:31:  bot, used both to verify inbound webhook signatures and to sign outbound bot-API
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-32-  replies. Set it as `webhook_secret`, which is canonical. `bot_token` is a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-33-  **deprecated alias for the same value**: if both are set they must be identical.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-41-mode:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-42-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md:43:- **Inbound**: signature verification is **mandatory**. With no resolved secret the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-44-  webhook endpoint returns `401` and never reaches the agent. There is no
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-45-  "public" mode that accepts unverified webhooks.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/nextcloud-talk.md-92-Local development? Configure `[tunnel]` in your config (ngrok, Cloudflare, or Tailscale) and the gateway exposes itself on startup: see [Operations → Network deployment](../ops/network-deployment.md).

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/introduction.md-3-Personal AI assistant you own, written in Rust.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/introduction.md-4-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/introduction.md:5:ZeroClaw is an agent runtime: a single binary you configure and run. It talks to LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and ~20 others), reaches the world through channels (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, email, voice, webhooks, your own CLI), and acts through tools (shell, browser, HTTP, hardware, custom MCP servers). Everything runs on your machine, with your keys, in your workspace.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/introduction.md-7-Read [Philosophy](./philosophy/index.md) to understand the opinions that shape it.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-16-## Cloud API mode
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-17-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:18:Cloud API mode is the Meta Business Platform integration. It requires a Meta Business account, a WhatsApp Business app, a phone number ID, a verify token, an access token, and an app secret. It is the right mode for business deployments that receive messages through Meta webhooks.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-19-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:20:Inbound webhooks are signature-verified against `app_secret`, and verification is mandatory. With no app secret configured the gateway cannot verify a request, so it answers `401` and processes nothing. Set `app_secret` before pointing Meta at the callback URL.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-21-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-22-The gateway must be reachable by Meta for inbound webhooks. Configure a tunnel under the top-level `[tunnel]` section (`tunnel_provider` and the related provider blocks, see the [config reference](../reference/config.md#tunnel)), or front the gateway with your own reverse proxy when developing locally.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-32-## Web mode
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-33-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:34:WhatsApp Web mode links a regular WhatsApp account through the optional Web backend. It does not need a Meta Business account. It does need a ZeroClaw build with the `whatsapp-web` feature enabled and a persistent session database path.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-35-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:36:On first start, the Web backend pairs the account using QR or pair-code linking (`pair_phone` seeds pair-code linking; leave it unset for QR). Keep `session_path` on persistent storage; removing it forces a fresh device link. Bind the channel to an agent via that agent's `channels` list.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-37-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-38-`push_name` sets the display name recipients see; leave it unset and the account keeps the name the phone was registered with. It is applied on connect, only when it differs from the name the linked device already carries, and a failure to apply it is logged without stopping the channel. Cloud API mode ignores it; there the display name comes from the Meta Business profile.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-50-| `self_chat_mode` | `true`, `false` | personal only | Controls the user's self-chat |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-51-| `mention_only` | `true`, `false` | both modes | Requires group messages to mention the bot |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:52:| `passive_group_context` | `true`, `false` | both modes | Records allowed unaddressed group messages as context only |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-53-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:54:`self_chat_mode` stays personal-only because the self-chat affordance is scoped to the personal branch by design. `mode` selects ZeroClaw's policy posture, not a WhatsApp account type: both modes drive the same linked-device session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-55-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-56-WhatsApp mirrors the linked account's outbound messages as `fromMe` events in either mode. Business mode drops these echoes before approval-reply handling or user-message dispatch, so they cannot start another agent turn. Personal mode retains its intentional self-chat and explicit operator-trigger handling; this business-mode rule does not remove those exceptions.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-73-notice a business-mode deployment gets.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-74-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:75:`passive_group_context = true` is opt-in and applies only to WhatsApp Web group chats. Allowed unaddressed group messages are stored in the room-scoped conversation history without starting an agent turn, sending reactions, downloading media, or calling the model. Later addressed messages in the same group can use that passive context.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-76-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-91-## Polls
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-92-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:93:The `poll` tool posts a native WhatsApp poll in Web mode instead of the numbered text fallback used on channels without native polls. The tool accepts 2–10 options; the WhatsApp library accepts up to 12, but the tool schema does not expose 11–12. `multi_select` lets a voter select multiple options.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-94-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-95-Raw phone-number recipients are checked against the channel's number allowlist, and a disallowed number returns an error instead of silently doing nothing. As with ordinary sends, JID recipients bypass that number check. `duration_minutes` does not expire a native poll.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-97-Votes are not read back yet: the poll card shows the result to people in the chat, and the agent only learns that the poll was posted.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-98-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:99:## Tool approval over chat (`approval_timeout_secs`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-100-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:101:When a tool needs approval (it is in `always_ask`, or the risk profile does not
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-102-auto-approve it), the agent posts the request into the chat the message came from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-103-and waits for a reply. Answer with the token from the prompt:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-111-`approval_timeout_secs` bounds that wait. **The default is 300 seconds, and `0`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-112-denies immediately** rather than disabling approval, so a zero is a way to refuse
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:113:every gated tool, not a way to wait forever. On timeout the request is denied and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-114-the token is discarded, so a late reply cannot approve a call nobody is waiting
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-115-on any more.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-146-In **Cloud API mode**, neither check is applied. Its pending entry is a bare
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-147-responder keyed by the token, with no chat and no identity recorded alongside
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:148:it, so the webhook treats possession of the token as authority. In a group that
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-149-means any member who can read the prompt can answer it, including from a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-150-different chat. Until that path is hardened, a Cloud-mode approval is proof
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-160-{{#secret-config channels.whatsapp.<alias>.access_token}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-161-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:162:The same applies to `verify_token` and `app_secret` (Cloud API).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md-163-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/telegram.md:288:| Teammates in one group or forum topic do not see each other's context | Group sessions are keyed per sender by default. Set `channels.telegram.<alias>.per_user_session = false` to share one session per chat (and per forum topic, when present). The shared session shares its controls: any member's `/new` resets the conversation for the whole group/topic, and a session-level `/model` override applies to every member, while `/stop` stays personal to each sender. Direct messages are unaffected. |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-1-# RFC Process
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md:3:An RFC records a durable project-level decision before implementation. The process exists to surface design trade-offs, give maintainers and contributors a chance to push back early, and leave a searchable record of *why* a decision was made.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-4-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-5-Most work does not need one. The RFC trigger is deliberately narrow so that proposals which genuinely need a project-level decision are not queued behind ordinary features.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-23-- a bounded implementation refactor.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-24-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md:25:Those go through an issue and a PR. A new channel, a new provider, a new tool, and a bug fix are all ordinary work, however large the diff. They need an RFC only when their substantive effect also crosses one of the four triggers above.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-26-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md:27:The test follows substantive project effect, not the issue title, the author, whether the draft was AI-assisted, or the mere presence of a migration, feature, or default change. When you are unsure, open an ordinary issue and say why you think it might cross a trigger. A maintainer can promote it; that costs far less than a stalled RFC.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-28-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-29-Security vulnerabilities are reported privately per [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/SECURITY.md), never as a public RFC.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-43-1. **Problem**: what user pain or system deficiency motivates this?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-44-2. **Proposal**: what are you proposing to do?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md:45:3. **Design**: the details; code sketches, schema shapes, migration plans
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-46-4. **Alternatives considered**: what else did you evaluate, and why not?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-47-5. **Non-goals**: what this proposal explicitly isn't trying to solve
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md:48:6. **Risks and mitigations**: what could go wrong, and what's the rollback story
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-49-7. **Rollout**: feature-flagged? schema-versioned? breaking change window?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-50-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-59-**Electorate.** An active Core contributor is a current Core Team member who cast an explicit ballot in a formally opened RFC vote within the preceding 30 days. Any current Core Team member outside that set may still ballot; doing so joins them to that vote's electorate and reactivates them for later votes.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-60-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md:61:**Ballots** are `APPROVE`, `REVISE`, or `REJECT`. `REVISE` withholds approval but does not veto. `REJECT` is a blocking objection and needs a specific reason. Your latest ballot before the recorded deadline for the current vote cycle supersedes your earlier one.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-62-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md-63-**Threshold.** Two-thirds of the final active electorate by default, rounded up to a whole voter. Quorum requires at least two explicit ballots; silence never counts toward quorum. Once quorum is met, silence from the electorate counts as `APPROVE` for ordinary votes. Unanimity is reserved for decisions whose cost or irreversibility makes a supermajority inadequate, such as license or legal-ownership changes; it requires explicit `APPROVE` from every assigned voter, and silence cannot establish it.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-8-## Desktop daemon capture
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-9-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:10:The Desktop supervisor captures daemon stdout and stderr into one bounded file: `<config-dir>/logs/zeroclaw-desktop-daemon.log`. `<config-dir>` follows canonical config resolution precedence: `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR`, then `ZEROCLAW_DATA_DIR`, then deprecated `ZEROCLAW_WORKSPACE`, then Homebrew/default resolution. The file is capped at 8 MiB; when output crosses the cap, the oldest bytes are compacted away and the newest tail is retained.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-11-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-12-## Config (`[observability]`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-13-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-14-Defaults: `log_persistence = "rolling"`, `log_persistence_max_entries = 200`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:15:`log_tool_io = "redacted"`, `log_tool_io_truncate_bytes = 40960`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-16-`log_llm_request_payload = "off"`. A fresh
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-17-install produces a 200-event rolling JSONL at
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-31-| `log_persistence_max_bytes` | `0` | Rotate once an append leaves the active file at or above this many bytes. `0` disables size rotation. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-32-| `log_persistence_rotate_daily` | `true` | Before the first event of a new UTC day, archive a file whose last write fell on an earlier day. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:33:| `log_persistence_max_entries_per_segment` | `0` | Rotate once the segment's non-empty line count reaches this cap. In steady state each archive holds exactly this many entries. When first enabled on an existing log, the file is archived whole (one over-cap transition); steady state resumes on the next rotation. `0` disables entry-count rotation. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-34-| `log_persistence_retention_max_files` | `7` | Keep at most this many archives; after a rotation the oldest beyond the cap are deleted. `0` keeps all. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-35-| `log_persistence_retention_max_age_days` | `0` | Delete archives older than this many days after a rotation. `0` disables age-based cleanup. |
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-42-If that sidecar cannot be written, retention removes every numbered archive,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-43-and the daemon then restarts, a sequence can be reused; an outstanding cursor
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:44:can consequently bind to newer history. Archives written before sequence
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-45-numbering existed keep their old shape (`runtime-trace.20260624-031500.jsonl`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-46-and sort before every numbered archive.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-122-> prefixes) are redacted. This does NOT guarantee removal of all secrets or PII. Prefer

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-128-### OTel Content Capture
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-129-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:130:OTel content capture is independent of log-based capture (`log_tool_io`, `log_llm_request_payload`). It controls what content is emitted as OpenTelemetry span attributes.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-131-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-144-- `full`: Content is leak-scanned but not truncated.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-145-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:146:#### Tool I/O
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-147-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:148:Controls `gen_ai.tool.arguments`, `input.value`, `gen_ai.tool.result`, and `output.value` on OTel spans.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-149-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-150-```toml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-151-[observability]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:152:otel_tool_io = "off"                  # off | redacted | full
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:153:otel_tool_io_max_chars = 1000        # per-field truncation limit
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-154-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-155-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:156:- `off` (default): No content attributes, only tool name + outcome.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-157-- `redacted`: Content is leak-scanned and truncated at `max_chars` per field.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-158-- `full`: Content is leak-scanned but not truncated.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-162-- Setting `*_max_chars = 0` is equivalent to `off` for that policy.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-163-- Content is always scrubbed (credential patterns + secret patterns) before truncation.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:164:- Truncation preserves JSON structure for tool arguments (leaf strings truncated).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-165-- Truncated fields get a `…[truncated {n} of {total} chars]` marker. The marker is metadata and does not count against `max_chars`: the kept content is exactly `max_chars` characters, with the marker appended on top.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-166-- Default `off` is a privacy-first change from previous behavior (feature-gated but always-on when enabled).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-167-- The content policy is bound to the observer/config instance, not to the process. There is no process-global OTel content policy: each `OtelObserver` derives an immutable content config from `ObservabilityConfig` at construction and consults it at the OTel export boundary. Multiple observers in the same process keep independent policies: a later observer cannot override or silence an earlier one's privacy setting (no last-writer-wins, no cross-observer drift).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-168-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:169:### Turn-nested memory and RAG spans (`observability-otel`)

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:173:attributed agent turn, so a full turn (memory recall, autosave store,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:174:LLM calls, tool calls) renders as one trace in Langfuse/Tempo. The three
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-175-events carry the same `channel` / `agent_alias` / `turn_id` triple as LLM
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:176:and tool events, exposed as `zeroclaw.channel`, `gen_ai.agent.name`, and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-177-`zeroclaw.turn_id` span attributes.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-178-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:179:Memory operations outside a correlated turn keep producing root spans: the

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-182-root span carrying the matching `zeroclaw.turn_id` attribute (full nesting
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-189-outbound prompt and conversation in addition to its `messages_count`. It is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-190-**off by default** and is a privacy-sensitive surface: when enabled, ZeroClaw
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:191:persists the full system prompt plus the entire conversation history on every
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-192-turn.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-193-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-194-| Value | What is captured |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-195-| --- | --- |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:196:| `off` (default) | No message content is recorded. The event still carries `messages_count` plus the always-on prefix fingerprints described below (`system_chars`, `tools_count`, and when present `system_sha256`, `tools_sha256`); they are digests, not content, but a trace reader can still test them for equality. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:197:| `redacted` | Full message history (role + content), credential-scanned with the same `scrub_credentials` pass used for `raw_response` and tool I/O, then truncated at `log_tool_io_truncate_bytes`. Truncation is flagged with `request_messages_truncated` and `request_messages_original_bytes`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-198-| `full` | Same credential scrubbing as `redacted`, but untruncated (replay fidelity, mirroring `raw_response`). |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-199-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-200-Every `llm_request` event also carries prefix fingerprints of the runtime's
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:201:request inputs, whatever the payload policy: `system_chars` and `tools_count`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-202-are always present; `system_sha256` (the first 16 hex chars of a SHA-256 over
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-203-the contiguous leading `system` messages, serialized as a JSON array of their
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-204-contents, present only when the first message has the `system` role) and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:205:`tools_sha256` (the same over the native tool specs serialized as a JSON
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:206:array, present only when tool specs are attached, so a reordered tool set
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-207-fingerprints differently). They describe what the runtime
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-208-handed the provider adapter, one row per logical request; provider-side
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-213-verdict: a changed `system_sha256` means one of the leading system messages
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-214-changed, or one was inserted or removed, for example after an included
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:215:workspace file changed, a before-call hook edited or added one, or the tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-216-framing switched between native and text protocol;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:217:a changed `tools_sha256` means the runtime tool-spec serialization changed,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-218-which includes metadata fields the wire does not carry. In text-protocol mode
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:219:the tool instructions live inside the system text, so `tools_count` is 0 and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:220:`tools_sha256` is absent while a tool-set change shows up under
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-221-`system_sha256`. Confirm an actual cache hit or miss from the provider's
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-222-reported cache usage. The fingerprints are counts and unsalted truncated
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-223-hashes, not content: they reveal whether an input changed and let a known
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:224:candidate text be tested for equality, but persist no message text. Anyone
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:225:who can read the trace can test a known candidate prompt or tool set for
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-226-equality, so treat trace files with the same access controls as the opt-in
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-227-payload capture that sits beside them.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-229-Both `redacted` and `full` always run credential scrubbing; the only difference
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-230-between them is truncation. The capture reuses the existing
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:231:`log_tool_io_truncate_bytes` cap rather than introducing a second one. Set or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-232-leave `log_llm_request_payload = "off"` to disable capture instantly, with no
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-233-redeploy.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-336-Restart from the newest page after changing filters. Treat `at_end: true` as the signal to stop requesting older pages for that walk.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-337-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:338:`at_end` is scoped to the segments the daemon could actually read. When a retained segment cannot be opened, or stops decoding mid-file (for example invalid UTF-8), it is logged, the unread part is left out of the merged view, and the response sets `incomplete: true`. The page is still returned, but `at_end` then means "no older events among the segments that could be read" rather than "no older events exist". Present such a walk as partial rather than complete. The same applies to a single-event lookup: rather than reporting a miss as `not found`, the daemon says the event was not found *and* that part of the retained history was unreadable, so it may still exist. An unresolvable segment cursor follows the same rule: when the anchor it addresses could not be validated because its segment would not open or decode, the end-of-history page carries `incomplete: true` too. Older daemons omit the field; treat its absence as `false`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-339-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-340-`until_line_offset` is a position in the current active file. Archive rotation, startup migration, and a configured path change replace the bytes or active file it refers to; restart from the newest page after those boundaries.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-342-`until_segment_cursor` is resilient across those boundaries, by different means depending on where the page ended:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-343-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:344:- **A page ending in an archive** is addressed by the archive's own identity, which is fixed when the archive is written and never reassigned to different content. Subsequent rotations therefore cannot invalidate it. If retention has since deleted that archive, the reader reports the history as finished rather than silently resuming at an unrelated position.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md:345:- **A page ending in the active file** carries an anchor event id alongside the offset, because the active file's path is stable while its content is replaced on each rotation. On resume the reader checks that the event at the cursor boundary still matches the anchor; on a mismatch it searches the retained segments for that event and resumes from wherever it now lives, so pagination crosses a rotation without duplicating or skipping events. If the anchored event is gone entirely, the reader reports the history as finished.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-346-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/observability.md-347-A cursor issued by an older daemon, which named a segment by filename without an anchor, is still accepted. That form cannot say whether it means a rotated archive or the active file, so the reader tries the archives first, where a name is never reassigned, and falls back to the active file.
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-21-- **Streaming replies.** The agent posts a draft comment and edits it in place as the response grows (edits are spaced ≥ 2 s to respect forge abuse limits).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-22-- **Reactions.** Acknowledgement reactions map onto the forge's reaction set (with GitHub: 👀 → `eyes`, ✅ → `+1`, ⚠️ → `confused`, …); unmappable emoji are skipped.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md:23:- **Cold start.** Events created before the daemon started are never processed, so restarting can't replay history. The flip side: comments posted while the daemon was down are missed, so mention the app again.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-24-- **Comment edits are ignored.** Only newly created comments and issue/PR opening posts trigger the agent.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-25-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-66-- **`sop` routing.** A `sop` route emits a channel-sourced SOP event with topic `git.<alias>:<event_type>` and a structured JSON payload. The routed event is consumed by SOP ingress rather than delivered as chat. Match it from `SOP.toml` with a `channel` trigger naming the channel and instance (`channel = "git"`, `alias = "main"`); the `git.<alias>:<event_type>` string is the channel-generated event topic, not a trigger field. Use an optional `condition` to narrow further, e.g. `$.event_type == "pull_request.opened"` or `$.repo == "octo/repo"`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-67-- **Mention gating per route.** The `mention_only` gate applies to conversational events on the message path. `sop`-routed events skip it: a PR routed to `pr-triage` is captured whether or not the author mentioned the app. Lifecycle/CI/release events have no mention surface and are never gated. The app's own activity is always dropped; other bots' activity follows `listen_to_bots`; every delivery passes the peer-group allowlist on the author's login.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md:68:- **Reply surfaces.** Comment, issue, and PR events reply onto their issue/PR thread. Workflow-run events reply onto the run's associated PR when the forge reports one; otherwise, and for releases, the target is the bare repository and the agent cannot reply on-platform (route those to a SOP or act through other tools).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-69-- **Events API backbone (optional, GitHub).** `events_backbone = true` additionally polls `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/events` with ETag-conditional requests (one request per repo per tick; an idle repo answers 304 and costs almost nothing). Caveats: the feed lags by up to ~5 minutes, payloads are trimmed, and **Actions events never appear in it**: workflow runs always use their dedicated endpoint. Anything surfaced by both the feed and a targeted endpoint is de-duplicated, so it's safe to combine. Gitea/Forgejo ignore this option today.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/git.md-70-
--

This regenerates the ignored TypeScript client and typechecks the dashboard without producing a bundle. The Rust lint/build/test jobs still use a `web/dist/.gitkeep` placeholder so the gateway crate can compile without the bundle. Producing a release artifact that includes the dashboard is a separate step:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:4:profiles, bundles, and MCP servers, plus a workspace directory on disk. Moving

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-14-│                             dropped refs, risk flags

--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-48-  new manifest does not describe is gone, rather than left to look like part of
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-49-  the bundle.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:50:- A failure the export reports, such as an unreadable workspace file or a full
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-51-  disk, leaves the destination as it was. The staged tree is discarded and any
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-52-  existing bundle is put back, so there is no partially written bundle to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-53-  mistake for a complete one.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-54-- A destination that overlaps a tree the export reads is refused before
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:55:  anything is created, in both directions and for the workspace and every skill
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-56-  bundle alike: an `--out` *inside* a source would have the copy consume its own
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-57-  output, and an `--out` that *contains* one would replace the tree being
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-58-  exported.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:59:- Retained identity-path components and skill-content directory names use a grammar that every supported target can materialize. That rules out separators and control characters, Windows-reserved names such as `con`, `nul`, or `lpt1` with or without an extension, and names ending in a space or dot. An unsafe identity path is removed. An unsafe skill alias remains in the config closure so the manual importer can rename or rebind it, but its content is not placed under `skills/<alias>/`; the manifest reports that omission. The root agent alias also remains unchanged in format 1, so rename a target-incompatible alias before copying the default workspace on that target.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-60-- The closure is proved before it is written. The rendered `config.toml` is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-61-  parsed back and put through the same validation the importing install runs,
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-80-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-81-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:82:Recover by renaming `.zeroclaw-export-old-<token>` back to the destination.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-83-Both directories are hidden and share the same `<token>`, so a crashed export
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-84-leaves a matching pair. A successful export leaves neither.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-98-  **keyless**;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-99-- the provider a carried runtime profile names in its own
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:100:  `context_compression.summary_provider`, which the agent never mentions but
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-101-  the target validates per profile;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-102-- every model-provider fallback reachable under the runtime's depth and cycle rules, also carried keyless;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-103-- the **content** of each referenced skill bundle, under `skills/<alias>/`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-104-  Skills live in the install-wide `<install>/shared/skills/` tree rather than
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:105:  the agent's workspace, so config alone would import an agent whose skills do
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-106-  not exist. Each bundle's own `include` and `exclude` filter the copy, so a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-107-  skill the bundle excludes does not travel.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-113-never advertises a `skills/<alias>/` tree it does not have.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-114-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:115:The test of the closure is that it stands alone: parsed on an install with no
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-116-other entries present, it passes `Config::validate()`.
