runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-127-| --- | --- |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-128-| `channels` | Names accounts and credentials that exist only on the source install. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:129:| `delegates`, `workspace.access`, `workspace.read_memory_from` | Name sibling agents that will not exist on the target. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:130:| `workspace.path` | A source-host absolute path. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:131:| `identity.aieos_path` | Kept only when it resolves to a file inside the exported workspace under the format's own path grammar: `/`-separated, no `..`, no backslashes, drive or UNC prefixes, or control characters, since the importing host may read those differently than the exporting one. A kept path is rewritten into that grammar (normalized, `/`-separated on every exporting platform), so the string in `config.toml` is the string that names the carried file. Paths into `memory/`, and paths whose file the copy did not carry, are dropped too. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-132-| `delegate_same_risk_profile` | Set to `false`: same-profile auto-delegation would otherwise reach agents on the target this one has never been paired with. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-133-| `risk_profiles.<alias>.approval_route` | Names a source-install channel and distinct approver. It is removed and reported so a same-named target channel cannot silently inherit approval authority. Removing it also removes the source profile's distinct-approver policy, so rebind one on the target before enabling the agent when that separation is required. |
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-135-| `a2a` | An outward-facing surface; the agent must be re-published deliberately. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-136-| `cron_jobs` | Not carried by bundle format 1. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:137:| `workspace/memory/` | The memory store. See below. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:138:| `workspace/MEMORY_SNAPSHOT.md` | The core-memory export the store re-hydrates from: memory in another form. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-139-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:140:### Memory does not travel
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-141-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:142:Bundle format 1 carries no memory, and there is no flag to opt in. The store is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-143-a live SQLite database in WAL mode: while the agent is running, its committed
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-144-state is spread across the database and its `-wal` sidecar, so copying those
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-145-files one at a time can capture a torn or stale database. A bundle is not a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:146:place to discover that. Carrying memory needs a real snapshot boundary, taken
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-147-through SQLite's own backup API against a quiesced store, which a later format
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-148-version can add.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-149-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:150:Both forms memory takes on disk stay behind: the store under `workspace/memory/`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:151:and the `MEMORY_SNAPSHOT.md` at the workspace root that an agent re-hydrates the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:152:store from. An imported agent starts with an empty memory.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-153-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:154:Symlinks inside the workspace are skipped rather than followed: a link's target
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:155:may sit outside the workspace, and it would resolve differently on the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-156-receiving host anyway.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-157-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:158:The source roots themselves are checked first. A workspace or skill-bundle
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-159-directory that is a symlink is refused rather than followed, because following
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-160-it would put the whole copy outside the tree the bundle claims to carry before
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-165-source that uses its default location is opened by walking each component from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-166-the install root (`shared`, then `skills`, then the bundle directory; `agents`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:167:then the alias, then `workspace`), each through the previous component's
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-168-handle, refusing a symlink at every step. A redirected `shared/skills` or `agents` is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-169-refused no matter where it points, even somewhere else inside the install,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-170-because skill content is only ever read through real directories under
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:171:`shared/` and a default workspace through real directories under `agents/`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-172-Symlinks *above* the install root are the operator's own path and are followed,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:173:with the same trust the config file's location gets. A `workspace.path` the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-174-operator configured elsewhere is exempt: there the configured location is the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-175-boundary, and only its final component is refused as a link.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-176-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:177:The workspace stays live while the export runs, since the agent that owns it can
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:178:be writing to it through an ordinary tool call. So the copy never re-opens a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:179:path by name. The workspace root is opened once, and every entry below it is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-180-classified *and* read through a handle on the directory that holds it, with both
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-181-steps refusing to traverse a symlink. That is what makes the skip a guarantee
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-189-one that was classified, compared by filesystem identity rather than by shape:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-190-an entry unlinked and replaced by a different host file would otherwise pass
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:191:every test, being a regular file with one link inside the same directory.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-192-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:193:Refusing the link matters even when it points *inside* the workspace. The bundle
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-194-has content boundaries of its own, and a link that never escapes the root can
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:195:still cross them: an admitted file replaced by a link to `memory/brain.db` would
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:196:carry the memory store under the admitted name, and an admitted skill replaced by
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-197-a link to one the bundle excludes would carry the excluded content. Neither
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:198:leaves the workspace, and neither is allowed.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-199-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-200-### Credentials
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-240-files travel; nothing inspects what is inside the ones that do.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-241-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:242:Each regular file that survives the workspace and skill filters is copied

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md:244:listed elsewhere on this page: the [memory store and its

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/portability.md-246-links](#exporting), skills a bundle's `exclude` rejects, and loose state at a

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-23-## 1. Requirements
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-24-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:25:Before testing message flow:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-26-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-27-1. The bot account is joined to the target room.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-28-2. Credentials authenticate the bot account: either `user_id` + `password` (recommended, see [§2](#2-configuration)) or an `access_token` (token path, [§3](#3-token-path-alternative-obtaining-access_token-and-device_id)).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-29-3. `allowed_rooms` includes the target room (or is empty to allow all rooms the bot has joined). Entries are matched literally against the canonical room ID (`!room:server`) of each incoming message, so list canonical room IDs here: ZeroClaw does **not** resolve a `#alias:server` entry for this allowlist. (Aliases are resolved only for outbound delivery targets such as cron `delivery.to`.) Find a room's canonical ID in its client (in Element: Room settings → Advanced → Internal room ID).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:30:4. A peer group authorizes the sender (`external_peers = ["*"]` for open testing, see [§6](#b-sender-allowlist-peer-groups)).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:31:5. For E2EE rooms, the bot can decrypt: a `recovery_key` (recommended) restores keys automatically, or keys are shared to the bot device manually.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-39-{{#config-where channels matrix}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-40-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:41:### Recommended setup: password + recovery key
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-42-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-43-The official, lowest-friction way to run Matrix is to let ZeroClaw log in
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-45-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-46-- **Omit `device_id`.** Let the homeserver assign one at login. ZeroClaw
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:47:  saves the assigned id to `session.json` and reuses it on every restart, so
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-48-  there is no value for you to look up, copy, or keep in sync. Pinning a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-49-  `device_id` by hand is the single most common source of broken key sharing.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-50-- **Omit `access_token`.** When it is unset, ZeroClaw falls back to password
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:51:  login. A fresh login is also what the auto-recovery path ([§8](#8-auto-recovery-from-corrupted-local-state)) uses, so the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-52-  bot self-heals from corrupted local state without operator action.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-53-- **Set `password`.** With `access_token` absent, `user_id` + `password`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-54-  perform the login.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:55:- **Set `recovery_key`.** This restores room keys from server-side backup and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-56-  cross-signs the freshly registered device automatically on every startup:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:57:  no emoji verification, no manual key sharing, no bootstrap. See [§5I](#i-recovery-key-recommended-for-e2ee) for how
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-58-  to get it from Element.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-60-So a complete recommended block sets `homeserver`, `user_id`, `password`, and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:61:`recovery_key`, and leaves `access_token` and `device_id` unset.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-62-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-63-The `access_token` + `device_id` path ([§3](#3-token-path-alternative-obtaining-access_token-and-device_id)) still works and is documented in
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-64-full for operators who must reuse a pre-existing token, but it requires you to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:65:keep a stable `device_id` yourself, so prefer password + recovery key unless
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-66-you have a specific reason not to.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-67-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-71-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-72-`homeserver` is required. For the recommended setup, also set `user_id`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:73:`password`, and `recovery_key`. `access_token` and `device_id` are only needed
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-74-for the token-based path in [§3](#3-token-path-alternative-obtaining-access_token-and-device_id); `allowed_rooms` optionally restricts which
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-75-rooms the bot answers in. Authorize senders with a [peer group](#who-can-talk-to-the-agent). Full field index: [config reference](../reference/config.md#channels).

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-78-> in Element. Going the token route instead? See [§3](#3-token-path-alternative-obtaining-access_token-and-device_id) for the password-login API

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-82-### About `user_id` and `device_id`

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-97-> [!IMPORTANT]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-98-> This section is for the `access_token` path only. If you followed the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:99:> recommended password + recovery-key setup in [§2](#2-configuration), you can skip it: you do not
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-100-> need an access token or a hand-managed `device_id`.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-137-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-138-- **Keep a copy of the token** when you first paste it. Secrets are encrypted at rest and `zeroclaw config get` will print `[masked]` for the token field; you can't retrieve it later. Stash it in a scratch note if you'll need it for the curl validation snippets in [§5C](#c-token-and-identity).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:139:- **Reuse the same `device_id` on every restart**: changing it forces a new server-side device registration, which breaks key sharing and verification in encrypted rooms. The auto-recovery path in [§8](#8-auto-recovery-from-corrupted-local-state) handles the rare cases where wiping is genuinely the right call.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-140-- **Rotating the access token later** without re-running the wizard: update the `access_token` field in your config (see [§2](#2-configuration)), then `zeroclaw service restart`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-141-- **Token shows as expired or invalid** at startup: mint a new one with the same curl, repeat Step 2.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-186-- The bot device must have received room keys from trusted devices.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-187-- If keys haven't been shared to this device, encrypted events cannot be decrypted.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:188:- Verify device trust and key sharing from a trusted Matrix session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:189:- `matrix_sdk_crypto::backups: Trying to backup room keys but no backup key was found`: key backup recovery isn't enabled on this device yet. Non-fatal for message flow; still worth completing (see [§5I](#i-recovery-key-recommended-for-e2ee)).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:190:- If recipients see bot messages as "unverified", verify/sign the bot device from a trusted Matrix session and keep `device_id` stable across restarts.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-324-- `Our own device might have been deleted`: harmless; old device is gone.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:329:**Prevention:** Don't delete the local state directory without planning a fresh login. If you need a fresh start, get new credentials first, then delete the store, then update config.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-330-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:331:### I. Recovery key (recommended for E2EE)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-332-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:333:A recovery key lets ZeroClaw automatically restore room keys and cross-signing secrets from server-side backup. Device resets, crypto-store deletions, and fresh installs all recover automatically: no emoji verification, no manual key sharing.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-334-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:335:#### Step 1: Get your recovery key from Element
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-336-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-337-1. Log into the bot account in Element (web or desktop).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-338-2. Settings → Security & Privacy → Encryption → Secure Backup.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:339:3. If backup is already set up, your recovery key was shown when you first enabled it. If you saved it, use that.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-340-4. If backup isn't set up, click "Set up Secure Backup" → "Generate a Security Key". Element shows the key (it looks like `EsTj 3yST y93F SLpB ...`); copy it somewhere safe.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:341:5. Continue past the key display: Element then asks you to **re-enter the key** in a confirmation box to prove you saved it. Paste it and continue to finish setup. This is the same value you put in `recovery_key`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:342:6. (Optional) Log out of the bot's Element session once the key is saved: click the account menu → **All settings** → Account, then **Remove this device**. Leaving it logged in is fine; removing it just keeps the device list tidy.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-343-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-386-Surfaces:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-387-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:388:- Session restore confirmation
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-389-- Each sync cycle completion
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-390-- OTK conflict flag state
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-410-- Always use canonical room IDs in `allowed_rooms`: aliases are not resolved for the inbound allowlist (they are resolved only for outbound `delivery.to`).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-411-- **Threading:** when `channels.matrix.reply_in_thread` is `true` (default), every bot reply lives in a thread rooted at the user's message. Top-level user messages open a fresh thread; existing threads are continued. The main room timeline only carries the user-initiated messages.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:412:- **Thread root context:** the first inbound message ZeroClaw sees in any given thread is prefixed with `[Thread root from @sender]: <root body>` so the agent has the conversation that triggered the reply. Threads the bot itself started skip the preamble. Tracking is in-memory only; after a daemon restart, the next message in each active thread re-injects the preamble exactly once.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-413-- **Inline-reply media:** `channels.matrix.mention_only = true` makes the bot ignore naked media uploads (no text body to mention against). When the user inline-replies to such a dropped event with a question (`@bot can you see this?`), ZeroClaw walks the reply's `m.relates_to.m.in_reply_to.event_id`, fetches the parent event, and pulls its media into the current message: the agent's vision pipeline sees the image even though the original upload was filtered out.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-414-- **Attachments thread alongside text:** `room.send_attachment` calls carry an `AttachmentConfig::reply(...)` with `EnforceThread::Threaded` when a thread anchor is present, so PDFs / images / voice notes land inside the bot's thread instead of the main timeline.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-415-- **Outbound media markers:** the agent emits `[image:url|path]`, `[file:url|path]`, `[voice:url|path]`, `[video:...]`, `[audio:...]` (and uppercase / `[document:...]` aliases) inside its reply text; ZeroClaw fetches the bytes (HTTP for `http(s)://`, local read otherwise) and uploads as the appropriate Matrix message event. **Missing or unreadable targets are non-fatal:** the channel logs a warning, drops just that marker, and appends a `(note: I couldn't deliver the file at <path>.)` line so the operator sees what was attempted instead of a silently-dropped reply.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:416:- **Voice messages** (MSC3245): inbound `m.audio` events carrying the `org.matrix.msc3245.voice` field are saved to `{workspace_dir}/matrix_files/` and run through the agent's configured transcription provider so the agent gets both the transcript text and the source path. Outbound voice notes upload as `m.audio` with the voice flag + zero-waveform set, so Element renders the bubble as a voice note; in an encrypted room the audio is encrypted before upload like any other attachment. See [Model Providers](../providers/overview.md) for transcription provider setup.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:417:- **Spoken replies:** with `tts.enabled` and the owning agent's `tts_provider` set, a reply is synthesized and posted as a voice note *alongside* its text, in the same thread, so the room keeps a searchable transcript either way. Which replies get spoken is decided by configuration, never guessed from the reply text:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-418-  - A sender in a `[peer_groups.*]` group with `output_modality = "voice"` on this channel. Matrix peers are named by user ID (`@user:server`, the form `peer-groups.toml` documents), matched case-insensitively with a leading `@` optional, and `["*"]` covers everyone. Both the reply path and the proactive path below accept the same shapes. Room IDs belong in `allowed_rooms` and are never peer identities.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-419-  - Proactive delivery (cron `delivery.to`, announcements) has no sender to consult, so a target room is voiced when one of its joined members belongs to such a group.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-421-- **Outbound voice markers:** the agent can also emit `[voice:<url|path>]` explicitly, which uploads that file as a voice note whatever the peer group says.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-422-- **Acknowledgement reactions:** controlled by `channels.matrix.ack_reactions` (default `true`). When on, the bot reacts with 👀 while processing and ✅ when done. Set to `false` to keep rooms reaction-free.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:423:- **Persistent sessions:** on first successful login, ZeroClaw writes `~/.zeroclaw/state/matrix/session.json` (user_id + device_id + access_token + optional refresh_token). Subsequent restarts call `restore_session()` from that blob: no re-login. The matrix-rust-sdk SQLite crypto store lives alongside it at `~/.zeroclaw/state/matrix/store/`. **Once `session.json` exists, rotating `access_token` in config has no effect until the file is deleted**: the saved token wins. Delete `session.json` to force a re-login from config values.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:424:- **Cross-signing:** when `recovery_key` matches what is sealed in your account's server-side secret storage, ZeroClaw runs `recovery().recover(key)` on every startup, the SDK imports your existing master / self-signing / user-signing keys, and the freshly registered device is automatically signed. **No bootstrap, no UIA, no key rotation.** If your account doesn't yet have cross-signing set up, generate the recovery key in Element (Settings → Security & Privacy → Secure Backup) before configuring `recovery_key`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-425-- **Cron delivery:** `delivery.to` should be a plain room id (`!abc:server`) or alias (`#room:server`). Older configs that wrote `<sender>||<room>` are tolerated: ZeroClaw extracts the last `!`/`#`-prefixed segment and warns about the malformed value.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-426-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-429-{{#streaming channel="Matrix" mode="stream_mode" path="channels.matrix.<alias>.stream_mode"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-430-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:431:Matrix specifics: in `partial` mode, tool-execution status is shown through the same edit pipeline as answer text. In `single_message` mode, tool/progress status updates are edited into one sliding draft while the final answer is sent as a separate Matrix message. `stream_draft_lines` controls visible progress lines: `0` removes only the line-count limit; it never creates a second progress message. `message_max_bytes` caps both draft and final event content, counting rendered Markdown (including generated HTML) and Matrix reply/edit relation metadata rather than only Markdown source. Oversized progress drops complete oldest lines or entries so the window retains newest activity; an oversized individual item is replaced by a visible alert. The separate final response retains a UTF-8-safe prefix. Progress content is escaped before Markdown rendering, so reasoning remains readable across lines while user/model/tool content cannot introduce Markdown or HTML formatting. Values below `512` use that effective minimum so a non-empty serialized Matrix event can fit. The budget does not apply to approval prompts, system notices, scheduled delivery, or other ordinary sends. Choose a budget below the Matrix event limit. `stream_reasoning` controls provider reasoning visibility in that progress draft: `off` suppresses reasoning-derived draft updates, `status` emits liveness ticks without raw reasoning text, and `full` emits raw provider reasoning text into the progress draft. `stream_draft_delete` controls whether durable progress transcripts are deleted before the final answer is posted; delete failures are logged and final answer delivery still proceeds. Placeholder-only drafts are removed before the final answer even when transcript retention is enabled. In `multi_message` mode each paragraph posts as its own threaded message, and the split is code-fence-aware, so blank lines inside fenced blocks don't break a code block across messages.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-432-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:433:`stream_tool_arguments` controls which tool arguments appear in `single_message`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:434:progress lines. Missing or empty configuration uses conservative per-tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:435:defaults; skill wrappers, plugins, MCP tools, and unresolved names show their
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-436-names only. A single `default_base` entry selects `none`, `safe`, or `all`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:437:while exact-name tool rules can replace that base or add and remove fields:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-438-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-439-```toml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:440:stream_tool_arguments = [
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-441-    { default_base = "safe", argument_chars = 60 },
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:442:    { tool = "delegate", base = "none", include = ["agent", "background", "prompt"], argument_chars = 0 },
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:443:    { tool = "mock_tool", base = "all", exclude = ["token"] },
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-444-]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-445-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-446-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:447:Rule order is irrelevant, duplicate tool/default entries are rejected, and an
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-448-omitted rule `base` inherits `default_base`. `include` adds fields after the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-449-base is selected; `exclude` removes them. Runtime-only fields are never shown,
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-455-In `safe` mode, only the recommended top-level scalar arguments are rendered;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-456-nulls, arrays, and objects are omitted. Selecting `all` or naming an argument
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:457:in `include` is explicit operator opt-in to compact JSON rendering of a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-458-composite value.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-459-`argument_chars` on the default entry changes the inherited per-value cap from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:460:`60`; the same field on a tool rule overrides it for that tool. `0` keeps full
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-461-values while `message_max_bytes` still bounds the rendered draft. Explicit
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:462:`all` applies to unknown tools; use an exact-name rule when enabling arguments
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:463:for only one extension tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-464-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:465:## 8. Auto-recovery from corrupted local state
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-466-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:467:The matrix-rust-sdk default SQLite store is single-device and assumes the local view stays in sync with the homeserver. Two failure modes break that assumption irrecoverably; ZeroClaw detects each at startup and (when `password` + `user_id` are both configured) auto-wipes `~/.zeroclaw/state/matrix/` and re-authenticates so a fresh device is created server-side.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-468-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:469:- **Orphan crypto state.** A `store/` directory exists but `session.json` doesn't (manual cleanup, interrupted prior install, etc.). Logging in fresh on top of orphaned crypto state reproduces `Duplicate one-time keys` / `SigningKeyChanged` conflicts that don't self-heal.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:470:- **`StateStoreDataKey::OneTimeKeyAlreadyUploaded` flag set.** The SDK persists this key into the state store the first time it sees a duplicate-OTK upload (per the SDK's own comment: "we forgot about some of our one-time keys. This will lead to UTDs."). It survives restarts; the only fix is wipe and re-register.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-471-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:472:**`device_id` drift is detected but tolerated, not wiped.** If `channels.matrix.device_id` differs from the device id stored in `session.json`, the channel logs a warning and honors the saved id (which is the value the homeserver actually assigned at login). Wiping on drift would create a recovery loop because auto-recovery itself generates a new id, leaving config and session permanently out of sync.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-473-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:474:When **`recover()` itself fails** (typically `MAC check for the secret storage key failed`), the channel logs the homeserver's default secret-storage key id, whether the key event has passphrase info, the whitespace-stripped input length, and the full error chain: these point at *which* layer rejected the recovery key without leaking the value. Recovery failures are **non-fatal** (they don't trigger auto-wipe); the bot continues, the new device just won't be cross-signed.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-475-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md:476:If `password` + `user_id` aren't configured, auto-recovery can't run: the channel bails with an actionable error pointing at the two choices: configure them, or `rm -rf ~/.zeroclaw/state/matrix/` manually.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-477-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/matrix.md-478-## See also

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/building-docs.md-19-- **Cleaning up:** `rm -rf docs/book/book target/doc` removes everything generated.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/social.md-85-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/social.md-86-1. **Restrict who the agent will respond to.** Gate inbound senders with a peer group (per channel, above): an empty peer set denies everyone, `["*"]` accepts anyone. This applies to every social channel, so an enabled channel with no peer group configured answers no one until you populate it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/social.md:87:2. **Keep autonomy level at `Supervised` or lower.** A public-facing agent in `Full` autonomy is effectively a public shell. For public-facing channels, restrict the tool surface in the global tool-policy config rather than expecting per-channel `tools_allow` (no such per-channel field exists).

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-1-# Service & Daemon
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:3:This page is the operations-side companion to [Setup → Service management](../setup/service.md); that page covers installing and uninstalling the service. This page covers running it: tuning, resource limits, graceful restarts, and multi-workspace setups.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-4-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-5-## Choosing between user and system scope
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-22-</div>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-23-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:24:Without lingering, a user-scope systemd service stops when the last session closes.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-25-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-26-## Restart behaviour
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-45-`SIGHUP` is ignored (the daemon stays running). A reload requested via the `/admin/reload` endpoint restarts the daemon loop in place rather than exiting.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-46-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:47:An in-place reload starts a replacement generation over the same durable sessions, so it waits for the RPC connections the retiring generation accepted to finish, including any agent turn still unwinding after a forced teardown. If that wait runs out of budget, the reload is refused and the daemon shuts down instead. The refusal is deliberate: exiting is what keeps a replacement generation from overlapping work that the old one never retired.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-48-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-49-How the daemon comes back after a refusal depends on what was running it:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-53-- When ZeroCode started the daemon itself, which it does by spawning an ephemeral daemon whenever it finds no local endpoint, ZeroCode owns that child and replaces it itself instead of waiting on a service manager. It makes a single automatic respawn attempt per disconnect, and flags the daemon as needing attention if that attempt does not come back.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-54-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:55:Conversation memory and session state are written to SQLite incrementally during operation, not buffered until shutdown, so a clean stop does not depend on a flush step. Tool receipts are in-band HMAC tokens in the conversation, not a separate on-disk log. A hard `SIGKILL` skips the clean channel teardown but does not corrupt already-committed memory; only an agent turn that was mid-write is lost.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-56-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-57-## Manual start for debugging
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-74-- Diagnosing startup failures that the service swallows
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-75-- Running under `gdb` / `lldb`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:76:- Testing a config change before committing to it
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-77-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-78-Terminate with Ctrl-C, same graceful shutdown semantics as SIGTERM.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:155:## Running multiple workspaces

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-157-Each ZeroClaw daemon owns one config directory (which contains its `data/` dir). To run two side by side, give each its own config directory via `--config-dir` (or the `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` env var):
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-168-</div>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-169-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md:170:Each instance reads its own config, its own `data/` (memory, sessions), its own gateway port (set per config), and its own channel bindings. Memory stays separate; a Telegram bot in one config dir doesn't know about the other.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-171-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/ops/service.md-172-`zeroclaw service install` always installs a single unit pointed at the default config directory; it has no flag to name or parameterize instances. To run more than one as a persistent service, hand-author a second unit file (copy `~/.config/systemd/user/zeroclaw.service` to a new name) whose `ExecStart` passes `--config-dir <dir>`, then enable it separately.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:3:This is the procedure followed when reviewing a pull request in `zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw`. It's loaded by the `github-pr-review-session` skill and read by human reviewers, it's authoritative for both.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-11-comments, branch names, commit messages, and check-run or workflow names. Do
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-12-not check out or execute code from a PR branch as part of a review. The existing

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-210-  when the PR fully resolves the issue; otherwise use `Related`, `Depends on`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-211-  or `Supersedes`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:212:- Behavior claims are checked against the controlling contract: the relevant architecture doc, source-of-truth module, trait boundary, existing test, public API shape, source comment, or explicit maintainer decision. Issue-fit alone is not enough.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:213:- Provenance claims are real. If the PR body, commits, docs, or review thread cite an RFC, audit, issue, PR, path, generated artifact, or follow-up finding, verify that the artifact exists and supports the claim.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:214:- Validation evidence names the checks being relied on: required CI, focused local tests, manual smoke, docs/link gates, or full workspace checks when broad coverage proves something narrower evidence would miss. Commands that ran include relevant output or an honest skip reason. Fresh required CI is valid evidence when it covers the changed surface; do not require duplicate local Cargo for the same head, target, and feature set. Pending CI is not evidence yet.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:215:- A presentation-sensitive visual change includes actual-interface evidence on an identifiable revision and privacy-safe screenshots at representative terminal or viewport dimensions with enough surrounding context to assess the result. Record numerical dimensions only when needed to reproduce or assess a concrete presentation concern, such as wrapping, clipping, or responsive layout. A semantic-only rendered-interface change may instead use exact-head automated evidence from the final supported-interface output when it cannot affect layout, styling, clipping, wrapping, focus, selection, or interaction behavior. That evidence exercises the real interface through its final renderer, observes the output users receive, and identifies the changed state and observed result; source inspection, pre-render composition, component-only snapshots, and helper-level assertions do not qualify. A concrete presentation concern restores the screenshot requirement. A noninteractive, unstyled, deterministic plain-text CLI, stdout, stderr, or log change may use exact output from the supported interface when it makes no presentation-sensitive claim and no reviewer has identified a concrete presentation concern. The evidence records relevant output-shaping context such as locale and terminal width. Interaction and transition claims also include the action and observed result.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:216:- Security/privacy, compatibility, rollback, and scope-boundary claims match
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-217-  the diff and current behavior.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-218-- Public text does not include bot/AI attribution footers, local workflow
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-219-  mechanics, private paths, unredacted sensitive logs, excessive raw logs,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-220-  irrelevant dumps, or stale lifecycle wording. Concise, relevant command
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:221:  output tails in `How I tested` are expected when the template asks for
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-222-  them.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-223-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-234-| A non-central semantic-only rendered-interface change lacks required screenshot evidence or qualifying exact-head final-interface output evidence | `--comment` and withhold approval until the evidence is supplied |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-235-| A semantic-only rendered-interface change has exact-head automated evidence from the final supported-interface output, cannot affect presentation or interaction behavior, and has no concrete presentation concern identified by a reviewer | Do not withhold approval solely because no screenshot was supplied |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:236:| A qualifying plain-text change has exact supported-interface output on an identifiable revision, records relevant output-shaping context, makes no presentation-sensitive claim, and has no concrete presentation concern identified by a reviewer | Do not withhold approval solely because no screenshot was supplied |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-237-| A reviewer identifies a concrete presentation concern in an otherwise qualifying semantic-only or plain-text change | Treat it as a visual presentation change and use the central or non-central screenshot-evidence row above |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-238-| You have nothing new to block on but other reviewers hold unresolved substantive concerns | `--comment` |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-258-Apply these rules in order:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-259-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:260:1. If `mergeable` or `mergeStateStatus` is `UNKNOWN`, refetch this state once.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-261-   If it remains unknown, stop this classification and do not approve on the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-262-   freshness-warning path; GitHub has not established whether the PR conflicts.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:263:2. `mergeable == "CONFLICTING"` or `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"` is a merge
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-264-   conflict, not a freshness warning. A request to refresh onto `master` does
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-265-   not downgrade the conflict.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-275-5. After excluding unknown state, conflicts, current failures, and evidence
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-276-   gaps, classify a request to refresh a branch that is behind current `master`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:277:   (`mergeStateStatus == "BEHIND"` or the comparison reports `behind_by > 0`),
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-278-   or to wait for the repo's required aggregate gate (currently
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-279-   `CI Required Gate`) when its `bucket` is `pending` on the verified refreshed

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-299-## Validation evidence gaps
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-300-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:301:An evidence hold withholds approval because required evidence is missing or stale; it is not automatically an author blocker. Reserve `--request-changes` for a gap that leaves the central behavior unproven, requires an author-owned code, design, or test change or author-only proof, or leaves materially false PR-body claims that a maintainer cannot safely correct from public exact-head evidence. Otherwise, name the missing evidence and withhold approval with `--comment`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-302-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-303-Correct or propose deterministic public-record repairs from public exact-head evidence as maintainer-owned cleanup, including stale validation wording. Do not turn them into author work or apply `needs-author-action` when the next step is not author-owned. Before treating screenshots from an earlier head as stale, apply the [behavior-preserving refresh rule](./user-boundary-proof.md#reuse-evidence-after-a-refresh).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-304-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-305-<!-- >>> generated:review-validation-evidence-gaps by `cargo generate review-docs` - do not edit <<< -->
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:306:When validation is the concern, identify the exact evidence gap instead of asking for "full Cargo" by reflex. Check the current required CI jobs and the changed surface, then ask for extra validation only where required CI does not prove the thing under review: tests for a platform that only received compile checks, Clippy for a platform or path outside the required lint job, desktop coverage when the desktop workflow did not trigger, release targets outside the PR matrix, stale CI beyond the base-drift-only case classified above, or unavailable CI.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-307-<!-- >>> end generated:review-validation-evidence-gaps <<< -->

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-309-## Shape and generated artifacts
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-310-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md:311:For `size:XL`, over-1k-line, or new channel/provider/tool-family PRs, review the diff shape before relying on CI or prior approval. The public review should say whether the size is justified, whether the slice is merge-justified now, whether it could reasonably be split, and whether the handwritten work is mostly new value rather than duplicated machinery.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-312-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/contributing/pr-review-protocol.md-313-Do not dismiss generated artifacts as harmless because they are generated. If a checked-in generated file affects policy, schema, routes, migrations, lockfiles, release artifacts, capabilities, packages, runtime behavior, or reviewer evidence, review it like source and ask the PR to explain the provenance when that provenance matters.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-1-# ACP: Agent Client Protocol
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:3:**ACP** is a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio that lets editors and IDEs drive a running ZeroClaw agent as a session host. Newline-delimited JSON, lightweight, streamable, easy to wire to a subprocess.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-4-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:5:Think of it as "LSP for agents": the editor launches `zeroclaw acp`, sends prompts over stdin, and receives session updates on stdout.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-6-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-7-## What you'd use it for
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-8-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-9-- An editor extension that offers an "ask the agent about this file" command
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:10:- A terminal multiplexer integration that opens a side pane with an agent session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-11-- A CI runner that drives the agent programmatically without a full gateway setup
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:12:- Anything that wants agent sessions without HTTP and without binding a port
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-13-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-14-## Protocol shape: v1
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-25-    "protocolVersion": 1,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-26-    "agentCapabilities": {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:27:      "loadSession": true,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:28:      "promptCapabilities": {"image": false, "audio": false, "embeddedContext": true},
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-29-      "mcpCapabilities": {"http": false, "sse": false},
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:30:      "sessionCapabilities": {"resume": {}, "close": {}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-31-    },
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-32-    "agentInfo": {
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-39-      "zeroclaw": {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-40-        "defaultModel": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:41:        "maxSessions": 10,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:42:        "sessionTimeoutSecs": 3600
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-43-      }
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-44-    }
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-46-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-47-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:48:`loadSession: true` and `sessionCapabilities: {"resume": {}, "close": {}}` indicate that session persistence is active. If the SQLite store could not be opened at startup, all three are absent or false and `session/load`, `session/resume`, and `session/close` will return `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` errors.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-49-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-50-`_meta.zeroclaw` carries ZeroClaw-specific extension fields not in the base ACP spec. Clients that only implement the base spec can ignore this object.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-51-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:52:`promptCapabilities.embeddedContext: true` means clients may send embedded `resource` blocks with a base64 `blob` in `session/prompt` (see below). `image` and `audio` remain `false` for now. Native ACP Image/Audio ContentBlocks are not advertised yet.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-53-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-54-The server always responds `protocolVersion: 1`. If you send a client-side `protocolVersion: 0`, you still get `1` back, v0 clients will see parse errors on the new message shapes; see [version compatibility](#version-compatibility) below.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-55-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:56:### `session/new`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-57-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:58:Open an isolated agent session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:60:**`agentAlias`** names which configured `[agents.<alias>]` entry to use. It may be omitted when a process, connection, or configured default supplies the alias, or when exactly one agent exists. Otherwise, multi-agent installations must send it explicitly. The alias accepts the camelCase `agentAlias`, the snake_case `agent_alias`, or the short `agent` form.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-61-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:62:When starting standalone stdio ACP, the command may carry **`--agent <alias>`**. When connecting through the **gateway WebSocket** endpoint, the connection URL may instead carry **`?agent=<alias>`**. These values are process- or connection-scoped defaults, not config changes. Alias resolution for `session/new` follows this precedence:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-63-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:64:1. explicit `agentAlias` / `agent_alias` / `agent` in the `session/new` params
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-65-2. standalone `--agent <alias>` or gateway `?agent=<alias>`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-66-3. `[acp].default_agent`
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-68-5. error when no alias can be resolved
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-69-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:70:Every resolved alias, regardless of which step selected it, must name an **enabled, dispatchable** agent. Unknown aliases and configured-but-disabled agents fail `session/new` with `-32602 INVALID_PARAMS`. A blank or whitespace-only process or connection default is treated as absent and falls through to the next step. Restore operations ignore both defaults so launcher or transport input cannot rebind persisted session ownership.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-71-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:72:The optional **`cwd`** parameter (aliases: `workspaceDir`, `workspace_dir`) pins the per-session file-access boundary, it becomes the `workspace_dir` inside the `SecurityPolicy` that all file tools enforce. It does **not** relocate the agent's own persistent state: per-agent plaintext state (`MEMORY.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `SOUL.md`) lives in the resolved **agent workspace** (`agent_workspace_dir(<alias>)`, i.e. `[agents.<alias>]` workspace), which remains an additional permitted root; shared SQLite stores and cron state live under `config.data_dir`. None of these is a single daemon-level `workspace_dir`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-73-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-74-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:75:→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/new","params":{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-76-    "agentAlias": "myagent",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-77-    "cwd": "/path/to/project"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-78-  }}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-79-← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:80:    "sessionId": "s-ab12cd",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:81:    "workspaceDir": "/path/to/project"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-82-  }}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-83-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-84-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:85:`cwd` is canonicalized on intake, `../` traversal cannot escape the intended root. An explicit `cwd` is honored exactly as the session boundary, including a narrower subdirectory under the agent's workspace.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-86-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:87:If `cwd` is **omitted**, the server uses the resolved agent's workspace directory (`[agents.<alias>]` workspace), not the daemon's launch directory. The one special case is a `cwd` that canonicalizes to the install root itself: clients such as Thunderbolt send `.` as a placeholder, which resolves to the daemon's working directory. That lone placeholder is treated as "no meaningful cwd" and also falls back to the per-agent workspace, so uploads and the tool sandbox stay out of the daemon root. Any other explicit path, including one below the install root, is pinned as given and never widened.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-88-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:89:### `session/prompt`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-90-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:91:Send a prompt. The response is a sequence of `session/update` notifications streaming back, terminated by the `session/prompt` result.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-92-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-93-The `prompt` parameter accepts either a plain string or an array of content parts:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-96-- **Array:** each element is a text part `{"text": "..."}` or an ACP resource block:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-97-  - **Text resource:** `{"type": "resource", "resource": {"uri": "file:///path/to/file.rs", "text": "<file contents>"}}`. Editor `@`-notation attachments with inline text.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:98:  - **Blob resource:** `{"type": "resource", "resource": {"uri": "file:///path/to/report.pdf", "mimeType": "application/pdf", "blob": "<base64>"}}`. Binary embeds (PDF, DOCX, images, etc.). ZeroClaw decodes the blob, writes it under `{session.workspaceDir}/uploads/` (SHA-named), and surfaces a marker in the agent prompt (`[Document: …]` or `[IMAGE: …]` for `image/*`). Maximum decoded size is **10 MB**; invalid base64 or oversize blobs return `INVALID_PARAMS`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-99-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:100:Parts are joined with double newlines in the order they appear. Blob intake is store-agnostic (it does not call RPC `file/attach`). The same materialization helper is used when MCP tool results contain `resource`+`blob` content (see [MCP embedded resource blobs](../tools/mcp.md#embedded-resource-blobs-in-tool-results)).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-101-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-127-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:128:`stopReason` is `"end_turn"` on normal completion and `"cancelled"` when the turn was interrupted by `session/cancel`. The ACP completion signal is `stopReason`; ZeroClaw also includes the current final `content` string for existing clients.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-129-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-130-Errors:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-132-| Code | Meaning |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:134:| `-32000` `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` | No active session with the given `sessionId` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:135:| `-32002` `SESSION_BUSY` | A prompt turn is already in flight for this session, wait for it to complete or cancel it first |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-138-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:139:### `session/update` notifications (agent → client)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-140-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:141:ZeroClaw sends four kinds of `session/update` notification during a prompt turn. The discriminant is the `sessionUpdate` field inside `update`:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-142-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:143:| `sessionUpdate` value | When emitted | Key fields |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-144-|---|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-145-| `agent_message_chunk` | Each streaming text token | `content.type = "text"`, `content.text` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-146-| `agent_thought_chunk` | Internal reasoning tokens (when enabled) | `content.type = "text"`, `content.text` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:147:| `tool_call` | Tool call initiated | `toolCallId`, `title`, `kind`, `status: "pending"`, `rawInput` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:148:| `tool_call_update` | Tool call completed | `toolCallId`, `status: "completed"`, `rawOutput`, `content[]` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-149-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:150:`toolCallId` on `tool_call` and `tool_call_update` are stable and correlated, the update completing a call carries the same `toolCallId` as the one that opened it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-151-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:152:The `name` field on `tool_call_update` is a ZeroClaw extension (not required by the base ACP spec). Clients can use it for display; it's safe to ignore.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-153-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-154-#### Delivering files to the client (`deliver_file`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-155-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:156:When the agent should hand a workspace file back for download or preview, it calls the **`deliver_file`** tool (`path`, optional `mimeType`, optional `title`). On completion, ZeroClaw emits a normal `tool_call_update` whose `rawOutput` / `body` stay small (a short human summary, **no** base64 dump and **no** machine trailer; every delivery field travels structurally on the typed tool artifact). The standard `tool_call_update.title` carries a human-readable chat label: the caller's `title` (any prose, e.g. `"Quarterly report"`) or the filename by default. The `content` array additionally includes a standard ACP embedded resource:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-157-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-158-```json
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-170-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-171-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:172:The `uri` is an opaque, content-addressed identity: `attachment://deliver/<sha256>.<ext>`, the full hex SHA-256 digest of the file's bytes. It is URI-safe and collision-resistant at the full 256-bit digest strength, and is never derived from the caller-supplied filename. The same full digest is the on-disk `uploads/` storage name, so distinct content never aliases one file or one uri. The same `uri` is carried structurally on the tool result (JSON field `uri`) and on the typed tool artifact; there is no machine trailer in the model-facing text. Before embedding the blob, the ACP layer re-reads the file and recomputes this hash, refusing to attach when it no longer matches; a swap between the tool's validation and delivery is detected, not trusted. Clients such as Thunderbolt materialize the outbound blob and build a citation ref-map keyed by that uri; agents must copy the returned `uri` into `<widget:document-result fileId="…">` / `[N]` citations and must not invent prefixes. The **chat display name** is the standard `tool_call_update.title` (the caller's `title`, else the filename). There is **no** `filename` field on the ACP `resource` object, and the `title` is display-only, never the on-disk name.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-173-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:174:The file must stay inside the session workspace (same jail as `file_read`); oversize files (>10 MB) are rejected by the tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-175-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:176:### `session/request_permission` (agent → client, outbound request)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-177-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:178:When a tool requires user approval (via `always_ask` in the autonomy config, or the `ask_user`/`escalate_to_human` tools), ZeroClaw issues a **JSON-RPC request** from agent to client. The client must reply with a result before the tool call proceeds.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-179-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-180-```json
