runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-209-- `{"outcome": {"outcome": "cancelled"}}`, user dismissed the prompt
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-210-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:211:If the client never replies (crash, network drop, user closes IDE), the request times out after `sessionTimeoutSecs` and the tool call is denied.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-212-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:213:`ask_user` uses the same `session/request_permission` mechanism, mapping the question's `choices` to permission options. Free-form (no-choices) `ask_user` is not supported until the [ACP elicitation RFD](https://github.com/zed-industries/agent-client-protocol/blob/main/docs/rfds/elicitation.mdx) lands. Calling `ask_user` without `choices` on an ACP session fast-fails with a clear error.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-214-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:215:### `session/cancel` _(ZeroClaw extension)_
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-216-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:217:Abort an in-flight `session/prompt` turn. This method is a ZeroClaw extension,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-218-not part of the base ACP spec. If ACP later standardizes a conflicting
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:219:`session/cancel`, ZeroClaw will move its extension to `_meta/session/cancel`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-220-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:221:**Cancel vs. stop:** `session/cancel` aborts an in-flight prompt turn and returns `stopReason: "cancelled"` with any streamed text accumulated up to the interrupt point. `session/stop` gracefully ends the session after the current turn completes, it waits for the turn to finish rather than interrupting it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-222-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:223:The canonical parameter is `sessionId`; `session_id` is accepted as a compatibility alias.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-224-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-225-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:226:→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s-ab12cd"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:227:← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:228:    "sessionId": "s-ab12cd",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:229:    "update": {"sessionUpdate": "agent_message_chunk", "content": {"type":"text","text":"partial..."}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-230-  }}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-231-← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:232:    "sessionId": "s-ab12cd",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-233-    "stopReason": "cancelled",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-234-    "content": "partial...\n\n[turn cancelled via client]"
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-236-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-237-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:238:If no turn is active for the session, the cancel is a noop, it succeeds silently without error. This follows ACP notification semantics: notifications must not produce errors.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-239-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:240:### `session/stop` _(ZeroClaw extension)_
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-241-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:242:Cleanly end a session. Not in the base ACP spec: ZeroClaw-specific. If a future ACP spec revision adds `session/stop` with different semantics, this will be renamed `_meta/session/stop`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-243-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-244-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:245:→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"session/stop","params":{"sessionId":"s-ab12cd"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:246:← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"result":{"sessionId": "s-ab12cd", "stopped":true}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-247-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-248-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:249:### `session/update` (client → server) _(ZeroClaw extension)_
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-250-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:251:ZeroClaw also accepts inbound `session/update` (and the legacy `session/event` alias) notifications from the client for custom event injection. Not in the base ACP spec: ZeroClaw-specific. If the ACP spec later defines an inbound `session/update` with different semantics, this will be renamed `_meta/session/update`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-252-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:253:## Session persistence
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-254-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:255:ZeroClaw automatically persists ACP sessions to SQLite. No configuration is required, the store opens at `<workspace_dir>/sessions/acp-sessions.db` whenever `zeroclaw acp` starts or a gateway WebSocket ACP connection is accepted. If the file cannot be created (read-only filesystem, bad permissions), the server falls back to in-memory-only sessions and `loadSession` reports `false` in the `initialize` response.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-256-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-257-What is persisted:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-258-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:259:- Session metadata: `sessionId`, `workspaceDir`, `created_at`, `last_activity`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:260:- Full conversation history: every `ConversationMessage` written after each completed `session/prompt` turn, in one atomic transaction per turn
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-261-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:262:Sessions survive process restarts. A session created in one `zeroclaw acp` invocation can be loaded or resumed in a later one, as long as the same `workspace_dir` is in use (and therefore the same `acp-sessions.db` file).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-263-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:264:Sessions are not automatically deleted. Use `session/close` to deactivate a session without deleting it, then `session/load` or `session/resume` to bring it back.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-265-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:266:### `session/load` _(ZeroClaw extension)_
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-267-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:268:Restore a previously persisted session with **full history replay**. The server seeds the agent with the stored conversation history, then streams that history back to the client as a sequence of `session/update` notifications before returning. The client receives the same update stream it would have seen had the session never ended.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-269-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-270-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:271:→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"session/load","params":{"sessionId":"s-ab12cd"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:272:← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:273:    "sessionId": "s-ab12cd",
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:274:    "update": {"sessionUpdate": "agent_message_chunk", "content": {"type":"text","text":"The last commit..."}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-275-  }}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:276:← ... (remaining stored messages replayed as session/update notifications)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-277-← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"result":{}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-278-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-279-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:280:After `session/load` returns, the session is active and ready to accept `session/prompt` calls.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-281-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:282:When restoring a persisted session, the server reuses the stored owner alias only if that agent is still dispatchable. Otherwise it falls back through the operator-controlled `[acp].default_agent` → sole-agent chain, skipping any disabled aliases along the way. Standalone `--agent` and gateway `?agent=` are `session/new` defaults only and do not rebind restore.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-283-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:284:`session_id` is accepted as a snake_case alias for `sessionId`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-285-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-286-Errors:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-288-| Code | Meaning |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-289-|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:290:| `-32000` `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` | No record exists for the given `sessionId` in the store |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:291:| `-32001` `SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED` | `max_sessions` active sessions already in flight |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:292:| `-32602` `INVALID_PARAMS` | Session is already active, call `session/close` first |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-293-| `-32603` `INTERNAL_ERROR` | SQLite read failure |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-294-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:295:### `session/resume` _(ZeroClaw extension)_
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-296-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:297:Restore a previously persisted session **without history replay**. The agent is seeded with the stored conversation history so it has full context for the next turn, but no `session/update` notifications are emitted. Use this when the client already has the history from a previous connection and only needs the agent state restored.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-298-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-299-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:300:→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"session/resume","params":{"sessionId":"s-ab12cd"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-301-← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"result":{}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-302-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-303-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:304:After `session/resume` returns, the session is active and ready to accept `session/prompt` calls. Same errors as `session/load`. Restore alias selection follows the same dispatchable-owner fallback rules as `session/load`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-305-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:306:**Load vs. resume:** use `session/load` when reconnecting after an unexpected disconnect and the client needs to rebuild its UI from the stored history. Use `session/resume` when the client already has the history (e.g., it stored it locally) and only needs the server-side agent state restored.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-307-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:308:### `session/close` _(ZeroClaw extension)_
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-309-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:310:Deactivate an active session: cancels any in-flight turn, removes the session from the in-memory active set, and unregisters the ACP back-channel. The session record in the SQLite store is **not deleted**, the session can still be restored with `session/load` or `session/resume` later.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-311-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-312-```json
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:313:→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"session/close","params":{"sessionId":"s-ab12cd"}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-314-← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"result":{}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-315-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-316-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:317:`session_id` is accepted as a snake_case alias for `sessionId`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-318-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:319:Returns `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (`-32000`) if the session is not currently active (it may still exist in the store).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-320-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:321:**Close vs. stop:** `session/close` deactivates the session while preserving its persistent record for later reload. `session/stop` also removes the session from memory but has the same effect on the store. Neither deletes the SQLite record.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-322-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-323-## Configuration
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-325-{{#config-fields acp}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-326-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:327:`default_agent` is consulted when `session/new` omits `agentAlias` and more than one agent is configured; if it is absent and exactly one `[agents.<alias>]` entry exists, that agent is auto-selected.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-328-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:329:When running `zeroclaw acp` as a subprocess, the command starts the server unconditionally. Add `--agent <alias>` when a launcher entry should default alias-less new sessions to one configured agent without modifying `[acp].default_agent`. When running as a daemon, the gateway exposes ACP over WebSocket at `/acp` with no additional config required. Gateway clients may append `?agent=<alias>` to that URL so each configured agent can be addressed from a spec-vanilla one-agent-per-endpoint client; authentication (`Authorization`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, or `?token=`) is enforced before the connection is upgraded, and the query parameter grants no access beyond selecting among already-configured agents.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-330-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-331-## Running

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-350-**Via the daemon gateway (remote or same-host):**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-351-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:352:Start the daemon normally. The gateway always exposes ACP over WebSocket at `/acp`, no extra config flag is required. Clients connect directly: for multi-agent installs, use a URL such as `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/acp?agent=myagent` so `session/new` can omit `agentAlias`, or through `zeroclaw-acp-bridge`, which bridges the stdio ACP protocol to the gateway WebSocket:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-353-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-380-## Version compatibility
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-381-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:382:ACP v0 clients (using the flat `{streaming, maxSessions, ...}` initialize response and `kind: "text"|"tool_call"` session/update shape) will see deserialization errors on connecting to a v1 server. The discriminants and envelope shapes changed in a breaking way. Upgrade steps:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-383-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:384:- Use `sessionUpdate` (not `kind`) to discriminate `session/update` notifications.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:385:- Parse `session/prompt` results as `{sessionId, stopReason, content}` (not `{finished, usage}`).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:386:- Implement `session/request_permission` response handling: the approval mechanism moved from a server notification to a client-answered RPC.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:387:- Drop the `systemPrompt` param from `session/new`, it is not read.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-388-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-389-## Security
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-390-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:391:ACP inherits the running config's autonomy level. When `[autonomy] level = "supervised"`, medium-risk tool calls trigger approval via the ACP back-channel, a `session/request_permission` outbound request the client must acknowledge. In `full` mode, uncovered tool calls execute without approval and `workspace_only` is implicitly disabled (the agent can reach paths outside the session cwd); tools listed in `always_ask` still prompt through `session/request_permission` (or fail closed if the client cannot answer). `forbidden_paths` still apply.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-392-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:393:The `cwd` from `session/new` becomes the `SecurityPolicy` workspace boundary used by all file and shell tools for that session. The agent's system prompt reflects that same effective session workspace: the prompt's "Working directory" is rendered from `SecurityPolicy.workspace_dir` (the session `cwd`, or the agent workspace when `cwd` is omitted), while the agent's identity and personality (`IDENTITY.md`, `SOUL.md`) are loaded from the separate agent workspace. The model therefore sees the directory its file and shell tools are actually rooted at.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-394-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:395:**Two-root file authority.** Setting the session `cwd` scopes *file and shell tool* paths (read/write/list, shell launch CWD, and embedded-resource `uploads/`) to that directory. It does not make the session an exclusive jail: the resolved **agent workspace remains an allowed root**, so the agent's own resources (skills, identity, and per-agent state under `[agents.<alias>]`) stay reachable regardless of the session `cwd`. In other words, `workspaceDir` controls where *session file operations* are rooted, while the agent workspace continues to back the agent's own config-scoped resources. When `cwd` is omitted (or is the install-root placeholder), the two coincide because the session is rooted at the agent workspace itself.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-396-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:397:## Memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-398-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:399:ACP sessions do not interact with the agent's persistent memory system. This is a deliberate design choice: ACP is for IDE-driven coding tasks, not long-term relationship building.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-400-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:401:**What ACP sessions inherit** from the agent config: personality, skills, risk profile, runtime profile, model provider, and all non-memory tools.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-402-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:403:**What ACP sessions exclude:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-404-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:405:- Memory tools (`memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_forget`, `memory_export`, `memory_purge`) are not available
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:406:- Automatic memory recall (the context preamble built from long-term memory at each turn) is disabled
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:407:- Automatic conversation auto-save to the agent's memory store is disabled
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-408-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:409:**Session context** comes from the persisted conversation history in `acp-sessions.db`. Sessions are persistent, resumable, and deleteable, the session history serves as the working context, not the agent's long-term memory.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-410-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:411:This separation ensures that ephemeral coding-assist conversations do not pollute the agent's long-term memory, and that unrelated knowledge from chat channels does not bleed into ACP sessions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-412-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-413-## Code reference
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-416-- ACP back-channel: `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/acp_channel.rs`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:417:- Session store (SQLite): `crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/acp_session_store.rs`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-418-- Gateway ACP-over-WebSocket endpoint: `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/acp.rs`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md:419:- Per-session path enforcement: `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs` (`SecurityPolicy::from_config`), `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs` (`from_config_with_session_cwd_and_mcp`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/channels/acp.md-420-- OS-level sandbox detection/backends: `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/detect.rs`, `landlock.rs`, `bubblewrap.rs`, `seatbelt.rs`

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:1:# Using Relationship Memory From Skills

It keeps the graph as an operator-facing workflow, not only an internal capability.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-34-Use this skill when the operator asks to remember or inspect how workflows, skills, capabilities, decisions, lessons, or steward roles connect to each other.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-35-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:36:Before writing graph memory:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-37-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-38-1. Confirm the deployment has `[knowledge] enabled = true`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-39-2. Ask what relationship should be remembered and why it should be durable.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:40:3. Ask whether the entry may include private workspace, account, client, or contact context.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:41:4. Refuse to store secrets, tokens, personal email addresses, phone numbers, private URLs, account IDs, session IDs, or credential-like values.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-42-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:43:Capture durable things as graph nodes with the `knowledge` tool:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-44-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-45-- Use `pattern` for reusable workflows, practices, or skill-shaped procedures.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:46:- Use `technology` for tools, protocols, providers, or capability surfaces.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-47-- Use `expert` for steward roles, maintainer roles, or agent roles. Prefer role labels over real names.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-48-- Use `decision` for design choices, policy calls, or accepted direction.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-134-## Project relationships
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-135-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:136:The same skill pattern can cover project or client relationships, but keep that as an explicit extension. Add `client`, `contact`, and `interaction` node guidance only when the operator wants project relationship tracking and has a privacy policy for that data. The [relationship memory](./relationship-memory.md) page shows the `client_network` and `interaction_log` actions for that shape.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-152-If your install root is not `~/.zeroclaw`, audit the path printed by `zeroclaw skills add`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md-153-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.md:154:`skills audit` checks the skill package shape. It does not prove that your deployment has the `knowledge` tool enabled or that the graph contains useful data. For that, run a small manual session with placeholder data and confirm the agent can call `capture`, `relate`, and `graph_neighbors` for a workflow/capability pair. If you extend the template for projects, also confirm `client_network` and `interaction_log` return the expected placeholder entries.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-30-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-31-- **`data/`** holds state that belongs to the whole install, not to any one
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:32:  agent: chat `sessions/`, runtime `state/` (cost tracking and the like), the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:33:  paired-device metadata in `devices.db`, and the shared instance memory under
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:34:  `data/memory/`. Valid gateway bearer tokens remain config state; `devices.db`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-35-  makes paired devices visible and manageable.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-36-- **`shared/`** holds resources agents draw on in common, notably skill bundles
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-37-  under `shared/skills/<bundle>/`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-38-- **`agents/<alias>/`** holds everything private to one agent. By default an
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:39:  agent's workspace is `<install>/agents/<alias>/workspace/`, and everything the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-40-  agent reads or writes stays inside it. The agent's identity source is resolved
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:41:  relative to this workspace. Agents are **jailed** to their own workspace
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-42-  unless you explicitly grant cross-agent access.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-43-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:44:## Workspace
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-45-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:46:The workspace is the agent's filesystem sandbox. The fields below are generated
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-47-from the schema:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-48-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:49:{{#config-fields agents.workspace}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-50-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-51-Two things worth calling out:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-52-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-53-- **`access`** is an inbound allowlist for cross-agent filesystem sharing. Empty
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:54:  means jailed (own workspace only); an entry grants a named sibling agent a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:55:  read or write mode into this agent's workspace.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-56-- **`unrestricted_filesystem`** is the escape hatch: when `true`, the agent can
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-57-  touch anything the host filesystem permits. It is off by default and flipping
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-58-  it on is auditable.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:60:## Memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-61-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:62:Each agent keeps its own memory store under its workspace
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:63:(`agents/<alias>/workspace/memory/`), separate from the shared instance memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:64:in `data/memory/`. The backend is selected per agent:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-65-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:66:{{#config-fields agents.memory}}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-67-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-68-The backend defaults to SQLite for a new agent, and once the agent has written
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-69-on-disk data the value is locked, so you cannot silently swap a backend out from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:70:under existing memory. Cross-agent memory sharing is opt-in through the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:71:workspace `read_memory_from` allowlist. Legacy string entries grant all
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-72-categories; structured entries can restrict a sibling to exact category
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:73:names on backends that preserve per-row categories. Markdown memory rejects
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:74:scoped grants because its files do not carry that attribution. For the memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-75-model itself, see
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-76-[Runtime internals](./internals.md). For a cross-system state map, see
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-85-The `format` selects how the identity is loaded. The default reads the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md-86-project's personality files; the alternative loads an AIEOS JSON definition,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/agents/filesystem.md:87:either from a path relative to the workspace or inline.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-1-# API Reference
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md:3:Full rustdoc for every public type in the workspace, auto-generated from the `///` comments on each type, function, and module. Use this when you need to know the exact shape of a struct, the methods on a trait, or what a function returns: anything the generated reference exposes better than prose can.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-4-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-5-**[Open the rustdoc →](/api/zeroclaw/index.html)**

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-7-## How to navigate it
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-8-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md:9:- The rustdoc index lists every crate in the workspace. Open `zeroclaw-api` to browse the shared trait contracts and boundary types.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md:10:- Use rustdoc's search box, keyboard search, or **All Items** to find a public name. Browser find searches only the current rendered page.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-11-- Click a trait to see its methods and known implementors.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-12-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md:30:| [`zeroclaw-tools`](/api/zeroclaw_tools/index.html) | Agent-callable tools |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md:31:| [`zeroclaw-memory`](/api/zeroclaw_memory/index.html) | Conversation memory, embeddings |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md:34:| [`zeroclaw-log`](/api/zeroclaw_log/index.html) | Workspace logging and observability integration |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/api.md-36-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-10-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-11-A plugin is a sandboxed WebAssembly module plus a manifest. The host loads it,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:12:reads the capabilities and permissions it declares, and exposes its tools to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-13-the agent only when the operator has turned the plugin system on. Nothing about
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-14-a plugin is implicit: a plugin gets exactly the capabilities its manifest
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-22-  no plugin code.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-23-- **Deny by default.** A plugin reaches a host capability (HTTP egress, config,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:24:  memory) only by declaring the matching permission in its manifest. An
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-25-  undeclared capability is unreachable, not merely unused.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-26-- **Verified by policy.** Whether an unsigned or untrusted plugin loads at all
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-30-## Lifecycle of a plugin load
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-31-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:32:When the runtime builds its tool set, the plugin loader runs through these
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-33-stages in order. A plugin that fails an earlier stage never reaches a later
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-34-one.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-45-4. **Enforce signature policy.** Each plugin is checked against the configured
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-46-   `[plugins.security] signature_mode` and `trusted_publisher_keys`. A plugin
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:47:   that fails the policy is dropped from the loaded set, not surfaced as a tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-48-5. **Admit executable bytes.** The host opens the confined component once,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-49-   verifies any declared `wasm_sha256`, and retains those exact bytes. In
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-52-   identity guarantee for the retained bytes, not a claim of race-free
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-53-   filesystem namespace resolution.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:54:6. **Register tools.** Surviving tool plugins are wrapped as agent tools and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:55:   appended after the built-ins. Tool dispatch resolves names first-match, so a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:56:   plugin tool that collides with a built-in name is never selected; give plugin
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:57:   tools unique names. Tool and skill plugins are *auto-discovered*, so this
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-58-   enumeration happens only when `[plugins] auto_discover = true` (default
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-59-   `false`, fail-closed): with `enabled = true` but `auto_discover = false`, no
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:60:   plugin tools or skills load, though channels you declare under
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-61-   `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` still activate. The skill loader applies the same
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-62-   `auto_discover` gate.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-78-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-79-In `strict` mode the manifest's `publisher_key` must appear in
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:80:`[plugins.security] trusted_publisher_keys`, and the signature must verify
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-81-against the canonical manifest bytes. Executable plugins must also declare a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-82-signed `wasm_sha256` matching the exact admitted bytes. A plugin that fails any
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:83:of these checks is dropped at discovery and never becomes a tool. The default
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-84-is `disabled` so a fresh local checkout works without key management, but a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-85-host that loads plugins from anywhere you do not control should run `strict`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-86-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-87-This policy is enforced uniformly: the same check that the host applies when you
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:88:list plugins is the check the agent runtime applies when it builds the tool set,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-89-so a plugin you cannot see in `strict` mode is also a plugin the agent cannot
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-90-call.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-94-A manifest declares two separate things, and the distinction matters.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-95-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:96:- **Capabilities** are what kind of extension the plugin is: `tool`, `channel`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:97:  `memory`, `observer`, or `skill`. A `tool` plugin contributes tools the LLM
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-98-  can call.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-99-- **Permissions** are what host services the plugin's code may reach at runtime:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:100:  HTTP egress, configuration, memory. A permission the manifest does not declare
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-101-  is a host function the plugin cannot reach.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-102-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-114-config surface (zerocode, the gateway, or the CLI):
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-115-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:116:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-117-# Master switch. Nothing loads while this is false.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-118-zeroclaw config set plugins.enabled true
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-119-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:120:# Load auto-discovered tool and skill plugins at runtime (default: false).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-121-# Without this, `enabled = true` activates only explicitly-declared channels.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-122-zeroclaw config set plugins.auto_discover true
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-134-A host meant to load third-party plugins should set `enabled = true`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-135-`signature_mode = "strict"`, and list only the publisher keys you trust. To load
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:136:auto-discovered tool and skill plugins as well, also set `auto_discover = true`;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-137-it is `false` by default, so `enabled = true` alone activates only the channels
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:138:you declare under `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and no plugin tools or skills. A
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-139-host that runs only plugins you build yourself can leave `signature_mode` at its
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-140-`disabled` default during development and tighten it before the host is shared.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-145-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-146-- It runs as a WebAssembly module with no ambient access to the host process or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:147:  the filesystem outside its rooted workspace. Network egress is gated by the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-148-  HTTP permission; the SSRF-guarded egress boundary itself is delivered by the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-149-  companion plugin-hardening work.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:150:- A trusted tool or channel plugin can read a schema-designated secret's
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-151-  plaintext through its scoped `secrets.get` import during an authorized
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:152:  service call. Tools receive access during `execute`. Channels receive
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-153-  `config.get` and `secrets.get` during `configure` and operational calls; reads
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-154-  within one call use one canonical revision, so a same-binding public/secret
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-158-  cannot prevent a malicious guest from retaining what it reads. Compliant
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-159-  channel plugins must resolve config and credentials at each point of use.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:160:- It cannot displace a built-in tool: the built-ins register first and tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md:161:  dispatch resolves names first-match, so a colliding plugin tool is simply
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-162-  never selected.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/developing/how-plugins-work.md-163-
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-83-### The Problem With Skipping the Top
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-84-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:85:ZeroClaw was bootstrapped by AI tools working from OpenClaw's TypeScript codebase. AI code generation works at the **Implementation** layer. It writes functions, structs, and modules that do things. It does not set Vision. It does not make Architecture decisions. It does not define Design contracts.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-86-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-87-The result is a codebase that is impressively functional but architecturally accidental. The code does what it needs to do today, but it was not designed. It accumulated. This pattern has a name in our industry: **the Big Ball of Mud**. It is the most common architecture in software, not because anyone chose it, but because it is what you get when you skip the top of the hierarchy.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-99-Breaking that down into concrete commitments:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-100-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:101:**Zero overhead.** The core agent starts in milliseconds and uses less memory than a browser tab. This is not a marketing claim. It is an architectural constraint. Every decision we make must be tested against it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-102-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-103-**Zero external requirements.** A user who downloads ZeroClaw and has an LLM provider configured should have a working, useful AI assistant without installing anything else. Channels, dashboards, and integrations are things you add when you want them, not things you need before it works.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-122-- The web dashboard (a full React application) is embedded in the binary using `rust-embed`, making every binary include the web UI even for users who only ever use the CLI
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-123-- The gateway HTTP server contains webhook handlers for WhatsApp, Linq, Nextcloud Talk, and Gmail, meaning specific channel integrations are baked into the web server
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:124:- Every one of the 70+ tools is compiled into the binary, regardless of which tools a user will ever call
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-125-- The only mechanism for excluding code is a Cargo feature flag, which requires users to have a Rust development environment and recompile from source
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-126-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:127:**The consequence for users:** The stated goal is a lean binary for $10 hardware. But the binary ships with code for 27 messaging channels, 70+ tools, a full web server, a React application, and integrations with Jira, Notion, Google Workspace, LinkedIn, and more, most of which any given user will never touch.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-128-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-129-**The consequence for contributors:** When a file is 9,500 lines long, it is not possible to understand it. When every feature is in one crate, touching anything risks breaking everything.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-135-| File | Lines | What It Does | What It Should Do |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-136-|---|---|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:137:| `src/agent/loop_.rs` | ~9,500 | Tool call parsing, streaming, history, cost tracking, model routing, memory, credential scrubbing, context building | Orchestrate a single agent turn |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-138-| `src/gateway/mod.rs` | ~2,260 | Web server + React app server + WhatsApp webhooks + Linq webhooks + Nextcloud webhooks + Gmail webhooks + pairing + rate limiting + WebAuthn | Serve the web dashboard API |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-139-| `src/providers/mod.rs` | ~3,750 | Factory + 40+ provider implementations + OAuth flows + credential resolution + error scrubbing | Route to a provider |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:140:| `src/tools/mod.rs` | `all_tools_with_runtime()` at L387–L1066 | Instantiate all 70+ tools unconditionally | Register the tools the user configured |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-141-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-142-**A 9,500-line file is not a module. It is a monolith that happens to have a `.rs` extension.**
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-146-This diagnosis should not obscure what is genuinely well-designed:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-147-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:148:- **The trait layer is excellent.** `Provider`, `Channel`, `Tool`, `Memory`, `Observer`, `RuntimeAdapter`, and `Peripheral` are clean, well-documented Rust traits. These are the right seams. The problem is they do not correspond to crate boundaries, so the compiler cannot enforce the layering.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:149:- **The WASM plugin system is partially built.** `PluginHost`, `WasmTool`, `WasmChannel`, `PluginManifest`, and Ed25519 signature verification all exist in `src/plugins/`. The execution bridge is a stub, but the structure is correct.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-150-- **The observability system has strong foundations.** OpenTelemetry and Prometheus are implemented against a clean `Observer` trait. The remaining work is to standardize how production paths emit through that interface.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-151-- **The security model is thoughtful.** Pairing codes, autonomy levels, sandboxing, and policy enforcement show real design intent.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-159-### 4.1 The Microkernel Model
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-160-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:161:A microkernel architecture separates a minimal, stable core from optional subsystems that extend it. In operating systems, the classic example is a kernel that only handles memory and scheduling, with everything else, filesystems, device drivers, network stacks, running as separate processes that communicate through a well-defined interface.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-162-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-163-For an AI agent runtime, the mapping reveals **two distinct internal layers** that the OS analogy conflates:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-165-| OS Microkernel Concept | ZeroClaw Equivalent |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-166-|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:167:| Kernel | **Foundation layer**: API traits, config, providers, memory backends, infra, tool-call parser. The irreducible core: builds with `--no-default-features`. Can exchange messages with an LLM and store memory. Nothing more. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:168:| Init / runtime system | **Agent runtime layer**: Orchestration loop, security policy enforcement, plugin host, core tools, IPC API. The `zeroclaw-runtime` crate, gated by the `agent-runtime` feature. This is what makes ZeroClaw an *agent*, not just a library. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-169-| IPC | Local socket / IPC API between the runtime and external components |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-170-| Device drivers | Channel plugins (Telegram, Discord, etc.) |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:171:| Filesystem drivers | Memory backend plugins (SQLite, Markdown) |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-172-| User processes | Gateway binary, Tauri desktop app |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-173-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-174-The distinction matters: the **foundation** is the minimum that must exist for any ZeroClaw binary to function. The **runtime** is the minimum that must exist for it to function *as an agent*. Everything else is composed in.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-175-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:176:This two-layer split was identified during the Phase 1 workspace decomposition (PR #5559) and is reflected in the crate naming: `zeroclaw-runtime` (the crate) is gated by `agent-runtime` (the feature). The earlier revisions of this RFC used "kernel" loosely to refer to what is now correctly named the runtime layer. This revision corrects that terminology throughout.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-177-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-178-### 4.2 The Dependency Rule

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-249-### 4.4 The Distribution Model
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-250-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:251:The architecture enables a clean distribution story that requires no Rust toolchain from end users:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-252-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-253-| User wants | What they download | What `zeroclaw onboard` does |
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-255-| CLI only | `zeroclaw` runtime binary | Configure provider, done |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-256-| CLI + Discord | `zeroclaw` runtime binary | Download + install `channel-discord.wasm` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:257:| Local web UI | `zeroclaw` + `zeroclaw-gw` | Configure both, open browser |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-258-| Desktop app | `zeroclaw-desktop` installer | Bundles runtime + gateway + UI |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-259-| Everything | `zeroclaw-desktop` or `zeroclaw --profile full` | Downloads all plugins |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-263-#### 4.4.1 Versioning Policy
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-264-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:265:As ZeroClaw transitions from a single crate to a multi-crate workspace, two concerns must be kept separate from the start:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-266-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-267-- **The product version**: what `zeroclaw --version` reports, what GitHub Releases, changelogs, and package managers (Homebrew, apt, cargo-binstall) track. This is the version operators and users reason about.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-274-##### Crate versioning: unified with intentional exceptions
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-275-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:276:All application crates, the kernel, the gateway, tool plugin crates, channel plugin crates, and the CLI use Cargo workspace package inheritance: a single version in the root `Cargo.toml` is the authoritative product version. This is the right model because:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-277-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-278-- Users, operators, and packagers deal with one version, not twelve
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-281-- The WIT interface version, not the Rust crate version, is the actual plugin ABI contract (see §5.2)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-282-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:283:Two crate classes are intentionally excluded from workspace inheritance and maintain independent versions on their own cadence:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-284-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-285-| Crate | Reason for independence |
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-297-|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-298-| **MAJOR** | WIT interface changes incompatibly (existing plugins must recompile); kernel IPC API changes incompatibly (gateway or external clients break); config file schema requires a migration; CLI commands or flags are removed or renamed |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:299:| **MINOR** | New capabilities anywhere in the workspace; new plugins available in the registry; new stable APIs; stability tier promotions; deprecation announcements (not removals) |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-300-| **PATCH** | Bug fixes; security patches; documentation corrections; no new capabilities and no deprecations |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-301-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-309-|---|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-310-| **Stable** | Covered by the product's breaking-change policy. No breaking changes without a MAJOR version bump and a published migration guide. | Kernel (target: v0.8.0), `zeroclaw-api` WIT interface (target: v0.9.0), kernel IPC API (target: v1.0.0) |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:311:| **Beta** | Functional and tested. Breaking changes are permitted in MINOR releases but are announced in the changelog with upgrade notes. | `zeroclaw-gw` (v0.9.0 → v1.0.0), mature channel and tool plugins |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:312:| **Experimental** | No stability guarantee. May break in PATCH releases. Must be clearly marked as `experimental` in docs and plugin registry manifests. | New tool integrations, new channel implementations, early hardware plugins |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-313-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-314-Stability tiers are **promoted, never demoted** through a deliberate team decision. Promotions are recorded in the changelog and, for architectural components, in an ADR. A component must hold its current tier for at least one full release cycle before promotion is considered.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-318-##### Release automation
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-319-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:320:Releases use [`release-plz`](https://release-plz.eplant.org/), which opens a release PR on push to `master`, bumps the workspace version, and generates a changelog from conventional commit titles. `release-plz` natively understands workspace inheritance and handles the crate publication order automatically. The independently versioned `zeroclaw-api` crate is managed separately using the same tool's per-crate configuration.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-321-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-322-#### 4.4.2 Release Artifacts
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:339:| **Retire → plugin** | `channel-nostr`, `channel-matrix`, `channel-lark`, `whatsapp-web`, `browser-native` | Removed from the kernel. Each becomes a WASM plugin crate published to the plugin registry. No compile-time decision required. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-340-| **Always-on** | `plugins-wasm`, `skill-creation` | Compiled into every kernel binary unconditionally. `plugins-wasm` is the kernel's core mechanism; `skill-creation` is a zero-overhead code path. Neither belongs behind a flag. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-341-| **Stay → platform/infrastructure flag** | `peripheral-rpi`, `hardware`, `sandbox-landlock`, `sandbox-bubblewrap`, `voice-wake`, `probe` | Remain as compile-time flags because they require native library linking or OS-level access that cannot be provided by a WASM plugin. `peripheral-rpi` and `hardware` appear only in platform-specific release targets. |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-356-- **`observability-otel`**: OTLP trace, metric, and log export carries a larger dependency footprint (opentelemetry + reqwest blocking client). Recommendation: remains opt-in, not in `default`. Production deployments that need native OTLP export enable it explicitly.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-435-### 5.1 Observability: OpenTelemetry
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-436-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:437:**What it is:** OpenTelemetry (OTel) is the industry standard for collecting traces, metrics, and logs from software systems. It is maintained by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation and supported by every major cloud provider and monitoring tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-438-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-439-**Why it matters for ZeroClaw:** We have already implemented `OtelObserver` against our `Observer` trait and expose Prometheus metrics. The issue is that these are not yet standardized across the codebase: some modules log with `tracing::info!`, others emit `ObserverEvent`s, and the two are not connected.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-441-**What we should do:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-442-- Adopt OpenTelemetry as the single observability interface for all components
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:443:- Ensure every plugin emits OTel spans when it executes, so a user can see a full trace from "message received on Discord" through "agent called shell tool" to "response sent"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:444:- Adopt W3C Trace Context (`traceparent`/`tracestate` headers) for propagating trace IDs across the kernel ↔ gateway ↔ plugin boundary
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-445-- Structured log output should be JSON when `ZEROCLAW_LOG_FORMAT=json` is set (already using the `tracing` crate, just needs a JSON subscriber)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md-446-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/zeroclaw-docs/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md:447:**Standards:** OpenTelemetry specification · W3C Trace Context (REC) · RFC 5424 (Syslog, for system log integration)
